Result and exact source scope

This draft gives a reviewed counterexample to extending the original eddy-current **ordinary potential correction** to every nonnegative bounded conductivity.

There is a smooth compactly supported scalar conductivity σ ≥ 0 and a smooth compactly supported divergence-free vector field A such that `div(σ(A + ∇φ)) = 0` has **no H¹-local scalar solution φ**. Thus the original gradient-valued map and its W(curl) electric-field reconstruction cannot be retained for arbitrary degenerate conductivity.

The conductor is a bounded connected Lipschitz toroidal domain with connected exterior. Conductivity is positive almost everywhere inside it but vanishes quadratically on one meridional cut. The proof uses genuine single-valued approximate potentials, strong weighted convergence and an admissible global divergence-free test field.

**The weighted-completion projection remains well-defined.** The result does not exclude every generalized or singular distributional potential, and it is not a separate all-forcing existence/nonexistence theorem for the full transient PDE.

## Complete proof and independent audit

- `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30001994/PROOF.md`

- A self-contained checker and its byte-reproducible 323-assertion receipt
- Seven unchanged independent-review files, including a separately authored 673-control checker

The uninvolved reviewer checked the full smoothness/topology, weak-test extension, weighted closure versus ordinary gradient distinction, the dual contradiction and all later-literature hypotheses. Verdict: **PASS_COMPLETE_ORDINARY_POTENTIAL_SOURCE_TARGET**, with no mandatory correction. All eleven author files and five primary PDF hashes match.

Original target remains unsolved (5/5)

This draft records five substantive attempts at OWR-14297732-013 / problem 30005584 and the independent review of the retained partial results. Neither the unrestricted expander degree of D³×S¹ nor the boundary-connected-sum degree law has been proved.

The original question is Eric Chen's joint-with-Bamler contribution in [OWR29/2023, p.1665](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/47471), repeated in OWR11/2025. [Bamler–Chen's full degree theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03154) supplies the moduli, spectral and localized-degree framework. [Rajan's published 2026 paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12220-026-02593-9) computes the cohomogeneity-one degree; its value is credited and is not promoted to the unrestricted degree. The full thesis comparison chapter also explicitly leaves that equality unproved.

## Retained scoped results

For the known complete S¹×R³ symmetric gradient-expander family, with the specified conical asymptotics, smooth-origin conditions and weighted L² form domains:

- Finite equivariant countermodels isolate invalid automatic transfers from a restricted degree to the ambient degree
- Circle-index parity and an exact weighted Hodge identity eliminate the entire circle-invariant reflection-odd negative space and kernel
- The circle-even operator has an exact Schur-complement reduction, including index equality and kernel correspondence
- An exact positive scalar transform gives H ≥ 1/√2 in the target normalization, together with a spherical-degree local bound on the Schur error

The effective nonspherical tensor sign, nonzero Fourier kernels, unrestricted full-fiber classification, full regularity, canonical orientation comparison and connected-sum gluing remain unresolved. Scalar-block coercivity alone does not establish them.

## Independent validation

An uninvolved reviewer returned PASS_SCOPED_PARTIALS for the unchanged author manifest `26ed40c1c0682d14c74fa2c2a94d7ba0cb247dde9423dd8d867cb5c4aea998a5`. All five receipts (177,000 exact controls) replay byte for byte; 4,538 separately authored exact controls pass. The full written weighted-domain, endpoint, Hodge-kernel, Schur and scalar-gap arguments were reviewed; finite checks are supplemental.

Result and exact scope
This draft gives a source-qualified affirmative transport characterization for problem 30001080 (OWR-2093-003), after two substantive author turns.

- On the original locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian framework, a sigma-finite joint law with a nonzero covariant locally finite measure is mass-stationary exactly when the entire joint law is invariant under every invariant, measure-preserving, measure-only Markov transport. Auxiliary state is retained; its measure marginal need not be sigma-finite.
- For the distribution of the measure itself, actual Cox-derived singleton matchings suffice when the original intensity measure remains available as background. The original OWR joint-object interpretation is explicit. A stricter allocation that may observe only the Cox configuration is outside this claim.
- The full OWR and foundational Annals texts were read. The final 2011 Cox paper could not be accessed; no theorem from that unread PDF is asserted. The proof directly constructs the stated kernel family.

## Proof and review
The frozen author packet retains the two-turn history, complete measure-theoretic proofs, atom/multiplicity treatment and Poisson-series appendix. Classical Mecke/Palm, invariant-transport and proper-metric inputs are credited.

A separate uninvolved AI reviewer issued PASS_COMPLETE_SOURCE_QUALIFIED_TRANSPORT_CHARACTERIZATION with no correction. The seven portable review artifacts are included unchanged. All frozen hashes match; 93,986 author exact controls replay, and 186,869 separate exact controls pass. These controls supplement the analytic review and do not replace it. Historical novelty and community acceptance are not certified.

The manifest's pending-review wording records the original freeze; the appended independent review is the later disposition. Only this problem's QUEUE row is changed to claimed_solved 2/5. Source PDFs, extracted text and private working material are excluded.

Result and scope

This draft gives a reviewed negative answer to the general fixed odd-power SOS-cone convexity question (OWR-12697710-006).

**The explicit example has degree 6, fixed exponent 3, and n = 3 × 10^62 variables.** It is a finite average of 10^62 disjoint copies of a modified Motzkin form. Every summand has an SOS cube, but the average does not. This does **not** settle the separately fixed ternary or any other prescribed small-dimensional case, and it is not a classification of all parameters. Closedness remains true.

The proof uses a rational order-nine moment functional with negative first seed moment. A finite tensor-product argument certifies separation of the cube of the block sum. The local 220-dimensional moment matrix has parity blocks of size at most 35; no astronomical numerical matrix or floating-point SDP is needed. The proof also gives an existential sufficiently-large-dimension consequence for each odd exponent q ≥ 3, with dimension allowed to depend on q.

## Proof, certificates and independent review

- `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30005460/PROOF.md`
- The author’s exact moment certificate, checker and 90,494-assertion receipt
- The unchanged first-turn scoped circuit and formal-preordering results and their 17,673-assertion receipt
- Eight independent-review files, including the complete 210 KB exact integer certificate and a separately authored standard-library checker with 210,525 controls

The uninvolved reviewer checked every leading principal minor of the full local moment matrix, additional two-block controls, the universal finite tensor argument, the known seed identity and the exact original arbitrary-n source scope. Verdict: **PASS_COMPLETE_GENERAL_NONCONVEXITY_SOURCE_TARGET**, with no mandatory correction.

## Scoped results
Five complete author turns establish an exact invariant-specific curve stabilizer obstruction, distinguish finite trace-algebra invariants from measurable ergodicity, construct a relative elliptic mechanism with a closed-surface lift, and compute its full six-dimensional twisted-cohomology action. Its relative two-dimensional invariant surface has zero ambient Goldman volume, while the four transverse eigenvalues form a hyperbolic reciprocal spectrum. This diagnoses that particular ambient elliptic route; it does not establish global ergodicity or rule out other nonergodic pseudo-Anosovs.

Counterexample to the literal unaveraged birational-map limit

The fixed map **L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v)** is birational over Q, with rational inverse (u,v/(u²+1)). For every prime **p≡3 mod4**, both directions are defined everywhere on F_p² and are inverse permutations. Every point lies on a cycle.

For the original point-weighted statistic D_p(x)=p⁻² #{z:T_p(z)≤px}, the unchanged proof gives, for **every fixed 1/2≤x<1**, limsup D_p(x)=1 and liminf D_p(x)≤23/24 along that same positive-density prime class. In particular there is no limit at x=3/4, nor any weak limiting cycle-length distribution. This is failure on an interval, not only at a possible limiting atom.

The argument combines exact fiber cycle counts, elementary character/Jacobi identities and the **unconditional** prime-average totient theorem plus Dirichlet/progression results. It does not assume GRH or Artin's fixed-base primitive-root conjecture. An arithmetic mean is a proof tool for extracting one subsequence, not a substitute for the source's unaveraged limit.

### Source boundary

Vivaldi's OWR54/2004 Conjecture1, pp.2944–2945, permits birational maps and suitable positive-density reduction primes. The example has a polynomial forward map and a rational inverse; it is **not** a polynomial automorphism over C. Narrower polynomial-inverse, elliptic-foliation and random-involution ensemble questions are not claimed resolved. No exceptional line or transient orbit is discarded.

Classical arithmetic and finite-field inputs are fully credited; historical novelty is not certified.

**Already solved, 0/5 author research turns.** Berdnikov–Guth–Manin, Forum of Mathematics, Pi12(2024), Theorem2.3 gives a negative answer to Gromov's2017 Question[?73][c]. The published theorem applies uniformly to every Lipschitz ball map, including unrelated choices as the radius grows.

For any fixed Riemannian manifold homeomorphic to #20(S²×S²), its cohomology cannot embed into the exterior algebra of R⁴. Rescaling the published estimate gives an R⁴/(log R)^α bound. Every fixed smooth fundamental4-form differs from normalized volume by an exact form, whose boundary contribution is O(R³). Thus the signed evaluation is o(R⁴), ruling out the requested positive lower bound.

## Scope and credit
This uses the original fixed smooth-form/controlled geometric-cocycle interpretation. Arbitrary unbounded algebraic singular cochains on noncycles are excluded. No scalar-curvature, formality, quasiregular or compatible-global-map hypothesis is added. No new theorem discovery or historical novelty is claimed.

Result and exact scope
A reviewed affirmative example for **30005468 / OWR-12697710-015**, the literal fixed-polynomial question in OWR14/2023 p.804. On a rational unit ball, a rational degree-four separator p=1+f has no certificate in 1+Q(g) whose square factors are rational, at **any multiplier degree**. The proof uses Scheiderer's credited classical quartic and a fourth-order Taylor-jet obstruction.

The scope is essential:
- This concerns one fixed supplied p, with min p=1 and a rational normalized moment vector whose moment matrix need not be positive semidefinite.
- The same vector has an easier rationally certified separator. A rational rescaling c*p with c>1 also has a rational certificate by Powers's theorem.
- Rational square factors (equivalently rational PSD Gram data) are required. Merely rational multiplier polynomials that are SOS over the reals are a weaker, unobstructed notion here.
- No strict-margin, all-separator, general Archimedean-descent or novelty claim is made.

The original report's own example permits min p=1; the companion preprint's stronger Corollary2 is explicitly distinguished. See SOURCE_SCOPE.md and PROOF.md.

Disposition
Already solved, 1/5 substantive author turns: a credited consequence of Grandis's established all-degree simplicial realization theorem, with the finite-domain and published digital-group comparisons written out and independently reviewed. No novelty claim.

## Exact convention-qualified answer
For finite reflexive symmetric digital images, use **strong/categorical adjacency on rectangular grids and homotopies**, with basepoint extension and fixed boundary. The groups D_n are defined directly from finite arrays, and the explicit functor F(X)=|Cl(X)| realizes them naturally in every degree. Degree 1 agrees with the published Lupton–Oprea–Scoville subdivision-based group; degree 2 agrees with the published Lupton–Musin–Scoville–Staecker–Treviño-Marroquín group, including its diagonal-block multiplication.

The original AIM Problem 1.3, “Topological realization,” presupposes a construction of higher groups. Independent source review accepts this as a complete **convention-qualified homotopy realization**. It does not assert agreement of every incompatible digital homology or homotopy convention; box-product A-theory and closure-space results are separately scoped.

## Attribution and proof
Grandis (Applied Categorical Structures 10 (2002), 99–155; complete author version arXiv:math/0009166, Theorem 6.6) supplies the established all-degree input. The packet proves the exact finite-rectangle/integer-net comparison, common support, caterpillar delays, negative-coordinate translations and group products. The published low-degree theorems and 2025 face-group work are credited. Current June 2026 McCord-source caveats are retained.

## Independent validation
The frozen 13-artifact author packet passed full independent proof and source review with no correction. All ten primary-source inputs match; 752,681 author diagnostics replay exactly, and 6,228,582 separate exact reviewer controls pass. These finite checks supplement the arbitrary-dimensional proof.

Status and exact scope
Unsolved after five substantive author turns. This addresses Dylan Thurston's Problem 12.11 in Ohtsuki's Problems on Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2002), printed pp. 533–536. The requested general condition on gleamed shadows that includes the alternating class and yields an exterior-volume lower bound remains unresolved.

## Reviewed partial results
- A conditional long-slope bound for specified subset fillings, with the actual exterior and cusp hypotheses retained
- A canonical alternating-shadow saturation criterion and a countercontrol to weaker sign tests
- A verified boundary collapse for a controlled alternating family, plus an obstruction to coercive raw-gleam/crossing lower bounds
- An essential-surface/guts reduction that subtracts the complete characteristic product contribution

These are scoped deductions using credited work of Turaev, Thurston, Costantino–Thurston, Ishikawa–Koda, Lackenby, Futer–Kalfagianni–Purcell, Agol–Storm–Thurston and Miyamoto. No novelty assertion or unqualified general-shadow solution is made.

## Independent review and checks
The unchanged 43-file author freeze passed a separate full analytic/topological/source audit. Five author outputs replay byte-for-byte (771,420 exact controls in total); the independent reviewer supplied 99,870 further exact controls. The proofs, rather than these finite controls, support the partial theorems.

Original problem 30005042 / OWR-9790363-001 remains **unsolved after five substantive author turns**. This draft preserves independently reviewed partial results. Only its QUEUE.md row changes, to unsolved 5/5.

## Reviewed mathematical scope
- Local X log(e+X)^(2+epsilon) moments imply almost-sure locally uniform and expected-supremum convergence of the exact coupled branching process. This permits offspring laws with no moment above one and needs no increment Hölder condition
- At the exact X log X endpoint: integrable smoothing-law uniqueness, integrated convergence, uniform scalar temporal-maximal control, and almost-sure common genealogical jump alignment in l2
- A certified rational continued fraction describes the actual geometric bivariate Laplace law. An exact mixed third moment excludes a matching-marginal/covariance independent-increment candidate

The cumulative small-jump/local-J1 tightness step under only X log X remains unproved. Simple full-process descriptions for the binary, geometric and Poisson examples also remain unresolved. The generic martingale countercontrol is not a branching-model counterexample. The scalar maximal estimate never moves the parameter supremum inside expectation.

## Sources and credit
Exact source: OWR12/2022, Mailler with Marckert, pp592–593, and the complete arXiv2106.01426v1 manuscript. Classical Kesten–Stigum, root decomposition, symmetrization and martingale inequalities retain credit. The final journal mathematical text was not verified: a Bath download has the correct cover metadata but an unrelated body, and is explicitly excluded. No historical novelty or complete-target claim.

Ohtsuki Problem 2.14 (M. Polyak), printed pp.408–409, asks for an appropriate recursively derived downstairs-link interpretation of integer Milnor invariants of based string links without assuming lower invariants vanish. This packet does **not** complete that original comparison.

## Independently reviewed partial results

- Exact lower-term and order corrections, including the distinction between integer based-string-link coefficients and closed-link quotient data
- An all-order integral relative-flatness construction with gauge-independent holonomy
- An actual properly embedded, possibly noncompact surface in a marked nilpotent cover whose intersection with a lower-data-corrected lifted final strand gives the specified integer Milnor coefficient
- Precise fixed-cycle and nonsplitting obstructions, plus the classical triple-invariant comparison in its stated vanishing regime

The covering-space formula is a geometric substitute, not the requested recursively derived downstairs link. The source allows adaptive, based and relative constructions; the narrow fixed-cycle obstructions do not rule those out. The original adaptive downstairs comparison remains unproved. No literature-wide openness or historical novelty claim is made.

## Full separate adversarial review

The independent reviewer passes all scoped results without a mandatory correction, after checking all five written arguments, source conventions, integral extension and gauge uniqueness, actual proper-surface realization, closing-word dependence and the exact limits of every obstruction. The final recommendation is **unsolved, 5/5**.

- Twenty-nine frozen author files and seven unchanged portable review files
- All 28 author manifest entries, six complete primary PDFs and five historical manifests verified
- All five author receipts replay byte-for-byte: 679,993 exact controls in total
- A separate reviewer checker passes 91,161 exact controls
- The controls supplement the full mathematical audit; they are not claimed to prove the general topology by finite testing

Bridson–Vogtmann Question 5.4 in the queue’s source edition asks whether the second Morita class has nonzero image under H_8(Out(F_6); Q) → H_8(GL(6,Z); Q). Kupers–Miller–Patzt, *The Morita classes are nonzero*, arXiv:2609.12951v1 (September 2026), Theorem A and §5.1 answer yes. This is credited existing work: **already_solved, 0/5 substantive author turns**.

## Independent audit and precise qualification

The separate full source/proof review passes the exact k=2 specialization, including the established Aut lift, its projection to the original Out class, the rational trivial-coefficient target, the (2,4) unipotent subgroup and the nonzero degree-eight pairing. Both KMP and its Ash–Miller–Patzt Hopf-algebra input are preprints as checked on 1 October 2026. This is not a claim of journal acceptance or community validation.

The required **CONVENTION_RECONCILIATION.md** is included unchanged. A literal scalar reading of KMP’s wedge-normalized twisted-apartment shuffle display mixes determinant-line conventions. The review states the invariant determinant-line coproduct, identifies it with AMP and the Reeder restriction map, and checks the nonzero pairing in those consistent conventions. This is not an accusation that Theorem A fails, and the inconsistent scalar reading is not endorsed. The k=1 zero-image exception is retained.

Credited literature relationship
Ohtsuki Problem 7.24 asks for the relationship between the original Borel quantum hyperbolic invariant and the normalized colored Jones evaluation. The literal 2001 definition has, for every nonempty link and odd N>1,

K_N^old(S³,L) = N^(-2N) J_N(L)^N.

The unknot-normalized version N^(2N) K_N^old equals J_N(L)^N. The scalar factor is essential: the original vertex factor is N^(-V), whereas Kashaev’s normalized closed state sum uses N^(2−V).

This is **already_solved, 1/5**, credited to Kashaev, Murakami–Murakami and Baseilhac–Benedetti. The packet supplies a source-convention dictionary, not a new all-link invariant theorem. It explicitly tracks the two tensor orientations, cancelling Clebsch–Gordan face gauges, Nth-root-only phase, later mirror convention, split-link zeros and the distinction from a general QHI with an additional sign ambiguity.

## Exact mathematics

The stable complex quadratics p_t(z)=(z+it)(z+t²-it) approach z². Their genuine full coefficient-space outward normals remain bounded. Comparing p_t with p_(sqrt(2)t) produces a positive cubic normal support defect but only a quartic squared coefficient distance. No uniform quadratic support bound can therefore hold at z².

The primary Poliquin–Rockafellar–Thibault finite-dimensional projection characterization proves that polynomials arbitrarily near z² have multiple nearest stable polynomials. The proof covers both the complex monic slice and all exact-degree complex quadratics, with an explicit six-dimensional normal and a justified closed-set localization. It also covers every fixed positive-definite coefficient inner product.

The abscissa epigraph separately fails set prox-regularity through bounded normals converging horizontally. Normalizing their height to -1 makes the coefficient gradients diverge, so this argument is **not** promoted to a counterexample at a fixed finite subgradient. The two stable comparison points are not claimed to be an explicit nearest pair for a displayed unstable input; nonuniqueness is an analytic existence conclusion.

## Source interpretation and credit

This field interpretation is an inference from the cited framework, not a quotation of an assumption printed in the short question.

The real-only restriction remains distinct: stable real monic quadratics form a convex orthant. The broader finite-subgradient function conjecture is not called resolved. Exact result

Claimed solved after one substantive author turn, with a separate full adversarial review. The original OWR question asks whether a contact process with fitness on a Galton–Watson tree can explode when the offspring mean is infinite. This is an affirmative existence result, not a claim that every infinite-mean law explodes.

Choose the almost-surely finite positive offspring law P(ξ≥m)=m^(-1/4), take constant fitness 1, infect only the root, use infection rate λ per directed edge and recovery rate 1. For every λ>0, the proof establishes

P(infinitely many vertices are simultaneously infected at time 1/(2λ)) ≥ (7/30) exp(-3/(2λ)) > 0.

This quantitative bound is annealed. A separate hereditary-subtree argument proves that for almost every tree and every λ>0, the quenched probability of explosion at some finite time is positive. No tree-uniform probability or explosion time, and no probability-one explosion of the dynamics, is asserted. Adding any finite fitnesses bounded below by 1 preserves the result, including the source's iid fitness model.

## Why the construction addresses recovery and explosion

The proof selects a descendant ray using only offspring data and arrows in deterministic shrinking time intervals. Newly inspected offspring/outgoing arrows remain fresh despite the bias in the selected vertex's own degree. The conditional first-failure estimates give ray probability at least 7/30.

Only afterward are recoveries restricted: the root and successive ray vertices have recovery-free windows with total length 3/(2λ). This has positive probability and leaves the whole ray infected at the same deterministic horizon. Each vertex is reached by an ordinary finite infection path in a finite ball. The proof therefore applies to the minimal graphical process, without assuming infection from infinity or treating a bare first-passage ray as sufficient.

## Source and credit

The exact question is Cardona–Tobón and Ortgiese's OWR 12/2022 contribution, printed pp. 618–620, question p. 619, DOI 10.4171/owr/2022/12. The neighboring moment-gap and bounded-offspring questions are separate. Constant fitness is allowed.

The latest July 2026 fitness manuscript's nonexplosion theorem explicitly assumes finite offspring mean; this example does not contradict it. Bartha–Komjáthy–Valesin (2026), Degree-penalized contact processes, supplies the finite-path graphical definition and a closely related growing-degree infection-ray mechanism for survival. Those methods are credited, with the simultaneous-infection recovery argument proved directly here. No novelty, priority, human peer review or proposer acceptance is claimed.

Claimed solved after one substantive author turn, with a separate full adversarial audit. The exact Table 5 target is the signed area of the pedal of the original billiard orbit times the signed area of its original antipedal, taken from either original focus. The product is constant along each primitive orbit family with period divisible by four and a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic. Primitive star windings are included.

All real antipedal vertices are finite. The focal pedal area is strictly positive in the chosen orientation; the antipedal area may vanish. This is a product theorem, and zero products are allowed without dividing by a zero area. The origin/odd-period k403,a row and the parallel k404 ratio are different targets.

## Proof and credit

The proof derives the actual focal line intersections and side projections, proves cancellation of the potential double poles including period four, identifies complementary cyclic dn traces, and establishes their half-real-period product identity on the reduced elliptic torus. Direct symbolic four-period geometry is included.

Classical Jacobi parametrization and compact-torus methods are credited. The overlapping even-period antipedal lemma was cross-checked with the parallel k404 author; SHARED_PROVENANCE.md records this exchange. That author was not the independent reviewer. No historical novelty, human peer review, or proposer acceptance is claimed.

Credited exact-source consequence

For a strict noncircular confocal ellipse pair and primitive **N divisible by 4**, including permitted star windings, the signed product of the **original-vertex unit focal-inverse area** and the **original focal-antipedal area** is constant.

This is arXiv:2004.12497v11, §3.9 and Table 9 p. 11, **k817** ([source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.12497v11)). The published companion omits this row; its shorter inverse table is not substituted. Both factors use the same original focus and straight-edged signed polygons, with no centroid, outer-locus-focus or elliptic-inversion interpretation.

## Proof and prior credit

[PR207](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/207) proves A times focal-inverse area is constant for this primitive parity. The general-even antipedal/original proportionality, now separately accepted in [PR255](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/255), gives antipedal area = kappa times A. Multiplication proves k817 directly.

Both full input proofs are copied unchanged and pinned in INPUTS.md. This is a shared-method, credited corollary, not a novelty or independent-discovery claim. The proposed campaign disposition is **already_solved, 1/5**, without asserting the exact general-N product was explicitly published in 2020.

All inverse and antipedal vertices are finite. **No derived area is divided by**: antipedal zeros are harmless and no nonzero-area condition is added to the product. The two foci have equal signed factors. Unit-circle normalization, reversal and repetitions of already-admissible primitive families are checked; the exact N=4 product control is 8.

## Separate full validation

The independent reviewer re-audited the entire PR207 input, verified its public bytes, and separately fully accepted the exact general-even antipedal lemma before checking this target. Independent controls: 5,433 exact and 3,822 separate diagnostics. Finite checks corroborate the proofs, and the AI audit is not human journal peer review.

## File scope

Only the frozen author packet, eight portable review files and QUEUE row 279 are changed. Complete source-target proof of **k404**: the signed area of the original orbit's focal antipedal polygon divided by its original-side focal pedal area is constant for primitive **N = 2 modulo 4**, including every permitted star winding in a strict noncircular confocal ellipse pair. Both original foci are covered.

All focal antipedal intersections are finite. The focal pedal denominator is strictly positive throughout the real family, so the quotient is defined everywhere under these assumptions. The antipedal numerator is allowed to vanish.

## Source and mechanism

Both arXiv v11 Table 5 p. 7 and the published Table 5 p. 348 specify this exact original-orbit ratio: [arXiv source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.12497v11), [published source](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/021-0174.pdf).

A direct focal-antipedal intersection formula has only adjacent original-vertex Jacobi poles. Central symmetry, reflection/reversal and the imaginary anti-period force the possible double area poles to be simple. Residue matching gives the general-even antipedal/original-area proportionality. The credited focal pedal trace aligns with the same trace at the requested parity; real positivity follows from the focus being inside the caustic and contact-normal increments below pi.

Stachel's canonical theorem, classical Jacobi identities, earlier campaign pedal-trace inputs and parallel shared-method work on the even-period antipedal lemma are credited explicitly in RELATED_WORK.md. Scope and disposition

Credited companion consequence for **5100016 / AMR-050-0016, k304**. Both arXiv v11 Table 4 and the final published Table 4 specify the signed-area ratio **A'/A'_M**, for primitive period N divisible by 4 and every fixed real M. Here A' is the outer tangent polygon's signed area, and A'_M is the pedal area formed by projecting M to that polygon's side lines.

The reviewed proof establishes a division-free identity A'_M = (c0 + c2 |M|²) A' along each strict elliptical-caustic family. The source ratio is constant on its natural domain.

- For convex families the pedal denominator is positive for every M
- For N = 4 the ratio is exactly 2, including the all-four-singular-edge complex-pole case
- An exact admissible primitive star family has a circle of fixed M for which A'_M vanishes identically while A' is nonzero. The raw quotient is undefined there; this is a domain qualification, not a refutation of invariance where defined
- Least-period, fixed-M, signed traversal areas and strict nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustics are retained

QUEUE marks only this target **already_solved, 1/5**, as a credited consequence of classical Jacobi geometry and the previously developed radial/pole mechanisms, not a new-discovery or historical-priority claim. Original target remains **unsolved, 5/5 substantive author turns**. This draft preserves independently reviewed, all-size partial results for selected generalized left semi-brace subclasses.

It permits arbitrary associative addition and completely regular multiplication, with the commuting local group inverse and possibly nonbijective Yang–Baxter maps.

## Retained partials

- Meet/retracted additions and arbitrary additions over left/right projection multiplication
- Coinciding laws in Rees presentations and the full one-/multi-column retraction parametrization, without imposing a false endomorphism necessity
- Exact existence and uniqueness for retractions across arbitrary Clifford components via greatest ideal idempotents
- Explicit rectangular and two-argument obstruction families, checking all three braid coordinates

**Remaining gap:** arbitrary two-argument associative additions and their interaction with general non-Clifford completely regular components. No subclass criterion, strong-semilattice construction, or finite catalogue is claimed to complete the source classification.

## Independent validation

The unchanged 28-file author manifest is `abccaf9cf1f2cb23cfce3b3127310f5cf9516acef87a0b05acc3692609eb1022`. An uninvolved agent's full mathematical/source audit returned PASS_SCOPED_PARTIALS with no correction. The review is an AI audit, not journal peer review or certification of novelty.

All five author diagnostic outputs and both bounded catalogues replay exactly: 436,129 author assertions. The separate reviewer added 2,760,310 exact diagnostic assertions, including nonfactorizing noncommutative Rees matrices and nontrivial Clifford quotient components. Finite checks corroborate the written arbitrary-cardinality proofs; they do not replace them.

## Provenance and scope

The original report and later generalized, inverse, weak and dual-weak brace papers are credited with their actual hypotheses. Source wording and access limitations are documented, including the right-zero/left-zero example convention discrepancy. No novelty or current historical-openness claim is made. Downloaded PDFs, extracted full texts, source images, complete imported records and exploratory files are excluded.

Original status: unsolved, 5/5

The exact K3 2026 Problem 1.17 asks whether an alternating link and a nonalternating link can have homeomorphic branched double covers. This draft preserves five substantive attempts and an independent adversarial PASS for the scoped partials. It does not claim a solution or novelty.

### Reviewed results
- Finite involution restrictions for hyperbolic covers and a determinant-one exclusion for common-cover constructions
- An integral deck-homology calculation and the precise missing equivariant push-in hypotheses in the definite-filling route
- All-links reductions to prime hyperbolic branch exteriors; the common closed cover may still be hyperbolic or toroidal non-Seifert
- An explicit toroidal L-space with an actual S3 branch quotient and no alternating branch, used only as a weak-criterion countercontrol
- Actual branching rigidity for the specified infinite two-trefoil-splice family: all branches of each cover are Conway mutants, so that family cannot give a mixed pair

The unrestricted hyperbolic/toroidal common-cover compatibility problem remains unresolved. The family theorem is not general graph-manifold rigidity. Classical inputs, exact BGH editions and source-access limitations are documented.

### Independent validation
The separate reviewer approved the unchanged full partial packet, with no mandatory mathematical correction. All 40 manifest-bound author files and 22 reading PDFs match their hashes; five author receipts replay byte-for-byte (361,240 finite exact controls). The reviewer supplies 56,947 independent exact controls and a full analytic/source audit. These computations supplement the topological arguments rather than replace them.

Thus the source ratio **A/A_M** is constant wherever its denominator is nonzero, including primitive star orbits and signed traversal areas.

Convex families have c2>0, so every real M is allowed. Star families can have c2<0: the exact k=1/4,N=10,turning-number3 family has an entire fixed circle of points M whose pedal area is zero for every phase. Every foot stays finite and A stays positive. Reviewed five-turn partials; original target remains unsolved

This preserves the independently reviewed research for OWR-14750-001 / 30003216. The original OWR contribution announces an augmented flux estimator but does not print its local formula, marking/coupling rule or delta policy. The full KLS2017 paper supports the corrected test-function divergence and a distinct primary-recovery estimator. The reconstructed procedures below have not been identified with that unprinted original algorithm.

### Scoped results
- Exact mixed reaction-diffusion equivalence, conservation defect and minimum-norm correction; a fine-only bias example calibrates an explicitly unaugmented residual
- A terminating variable-delta planar RT0 variant with absolute defect tolerance, edge marking and data-oscillation refinement
- A fixed-delta planar P1/RT0 two-mesh variant with separate primary/fine marking and fine-over-coarse overlay, converging in H1 and H(div)
- On convex polygons, a flux upper estimator with tangential terms, data oscillation and a higher-order coarse contribution; it converges under the specified fixed-delta variant

The algorithm results require A=I, homogeneous Dirichlet data, exact solves/integration and the stated nested, uniformly shape-regular refinement rules. Domain hypotheses differ by theorem and remain explicit. No claim covers arbitrary policies, three dimensions, general coefficients, higher-order elements, inexact solvers, rates or optimal complexity. The fine-only example is not a counterexample to the source's augmented estimator. Classical inputs and the existing Uzawa/reduced-mixed literature are credited; no novelty claim is made.

### Independent verification
The separate full analytic and source audit passed all five scoped results without revisions and retained the original unsolved status.

Complete credited construction

Ohtsuki Problem 5.9 is answered by combining the published Carter–Elhamdadi–Graña–Saito generalized cocycle invariant with the exact pullback obstruction to lifting a knot-quandle coloring. A finite diagram supplies an affine lifting system, and a fiberwise gauge matches the original coefficient convention to the published one.

Campaign disposition: **already_solved, 1/5**, as a standard-theory consequence. This is not a novelty claim, and we do not assert that this exact two-variable packaging appeared in 2005.

- The scalar published theorem gives a necessary obstruction only. Exact liftability comes from the separately proved pullback/affine criterion.
- Finite X gives a finite state sum with arbitrary abelian coefficient group A. Arbitrary X is handled by an indexed family; no invalid infinite group-ring sum is used.
- Setting the extra variable to 1 recovers the published generalized invariant, and trivial action recovers the ordinary cocycle invariant.
- Independent full review passed unchanged. The reviewer also gives an explicit zero-scalar-weight coloring that does not lift, confirming why the extra test matters.
- 138,333 author and 179,217 independent exact controls pass. These diagnostics supplement the analytic proofs and full primary-source audit.

Original source: [Ohtsuki, GT Monographs 4 (2002), printed pp.463–464](https://msp.org/gtm/2002/04/gtm-2002-04-024s.pdf). Published input: [Carter–Elhamdadi–Graña–Saito, Osaka J. Math. 42 (2005), pp.521–525](https://www.i-repository.net/contents/osakacu/sugaku/111F0000002-04203-1.pdf).

The PR includes the unchanged frozen author packet, seven portable independent-review files, and only queue row262. Outcome: original problem remains unsolved after 5/5 turns

This is a reviewed partial research packet for **30006395 / OWR-14299518-013**, Nina Kamčev's unknown-template planted-tree question in OWR 42/2025, printed pp.2267–2269. It does **not** identify the sharp information-theoretic transition or settle the source's logarithmic-size and computational questions.

### Exact model and verified partial results
The null is G(n,c/n). The alternative chooses a uniform k-subset and a uniform labelled Cayley tree on it, forces the tree's edges, and leaves all other edges independent with probability c/n. The test is not given the tree shape or its embedding. Results for a revealed fixed template are not silently substituted.

- An exact forest expansion gives the likelihood-ratio second moment. For fixed c>e, total variation tends to zero when k=o(sqrt(n)); an edge-count test detects when k grows faster than sqrt(n).
- For fixed c>e and k/sqrt(n) tending to a finite constant, the packet proves the likelihood-ratio lognormal limit and the corresponding total-variation/testing-risk limit, with a uniform L2 approximation argument.
- At c=e, the k^(9/4)/n critical window and its near-critical deformation are **second-moment results**. The scale n^(4/9) is not asserted to be the information-theoretic detection threshold. Divergence of the second moment is not used as a detection proof.
- A constructive fixed-depth branch-likelihood scan proves detection at c=3/2 when **k/log^2(n) tends to infinity**, using an exact rational entropy certificate. This is not the stronger fixed-C log-squared statement announced at smaller c in the source, and the exhaustive scan is not claimed polynomial-time.

The resulting polylogarithmic-detection boundary is confined to [3/2,e]. Its value, behavior in the remaining gap, the critical c=e testing law, and the original logarithmic/computational questions remain unresolved.

### Independent adversarial review
A separate reviewer returned **PASS_SCOPED_PARTIALS_ORIGINAL_UNSOLVED_5_OF_5**, with no mandatory correction. The audit checks the exact source model, critical dominated limits, diagram/Wick and uniform-tail arguments, the selected-root Cayley coupling, and the multiplicative null bound needed for the scan.

Problem 30001321 / OWR-4081-005, rank 253. The attached proof establishes the **positive one-transverse-dimensional analogue** of Berger's theorem in OWR 38/2009, printed pp.2151–2152. This is contrary to the negative Conjecture 1 printed immediately afterward.

For every fixed iid space-time law with 0<p<1 almost surely, every deterministic diverging interval scale M_N, every deterministic alignment, and every fixed epsilon>0, the environmental probability that the coarse endpoint L1 discrepancy exceeds epsilon decays faster than every power of N.

- Merely elliptic laws are allowed; no common uniform ellipticity constant or inverse-moment assumption
- Constants depend on the fixed law; no uniformity as the law approaches a degenerate random-arrow law
- Arbitrarily slow divergence is covered, not only polynomial scales
- Same-parity nearest-neighbor coupling and biased drift are explicit
- Both integer lattice intervals and the real half-open interval-length reading are covered
- No claim for static environments or environment-adapted partitions

QUEUE.md changes only this row to **claimed_solved, 3/5**. This is a mathematical research claim supported by separate AI adversarial review, not human peer review or a historical novelty certification.

## Proof structure

1. Exact sticky replica-chain and layer-martingale estimates give coarse expectation convergence at every diverging scale
2. All-order occupation moments and common variance control give superpolynomial tails at fixed auxiliary scales above N^(1/4)
3. A mesoscopic final segment uses same-parity coalescing coupling, small incoming strip masses, and bounded differences over independent moving environment strips to close the arbitrary-scale gap

The target scale enters only an expectation term tending to zero. The concentration exponent does not require a quantitative growth rate for it. All analytic dependencies are included in the frozen first two turn files.

Scope and disposition

Problem 30003427 / OWR-15218-003, rank 259. This is a credited classical-consequence, algorithmic answer to the original finite-data multiple-maturity question. QUEUE.md changes only this row to **already_solved, 1/5**.

For q quoted calls at T dates, conditional Carathéodory compression gives a uniform (q+2)^T-leaf model bound. The attached explicit quadratic system is equivalent to the source's finite-market definition, preserving the separate adapted settlement reference and shadow martingale, positive bid prices, the reference lower bound, deterministic discounting, and the initial spread. Classical real quantifier elimination removes the model variables.

- Rational or real-algebraic inputs: a terminating exact algorithm characterizes the full admissible spread-bound set, and decides its minimum or nonattained infimum
- Arbitrary real parameters: a formal semialgebraic characterization; no finite-bit algorithm on unspecified noncomputable reals is claimed
- An exact two-maturity example shows that strict positivity can give infimum zero without an admissible minimum
- No practical complexity bound, short calendar-inequality formula, general CAD execution, financial recommendation, or historical novelty claim

## Credit and original scope

The source is Gerhold's joint contribution with Gülüm, OWR 13/2017, printed p.697. Gerhold–Gülüm retain full credit for the model, one-maturity results and peacock formulations. The proof credits classical conditional Carathéodory/martingale Tchakaloff compression (including Beiglböck–Nutz) and effective Tarski–Seidenberg elimination. Lee's July 2026 two-date basket preprint is identified as separate prior work; its basket claims are not assumed here.

This answers the literal arbitrary-finite-maturity characterization algorithmically. It does not claim a resolution of a different calendar-vertical-basket sufficiency or arbitrage-classification conjecture.

**Original target remains unsolved after 5/5 substantive author turns.** This is a reviewed partial-results packet for 30000661 / OWR-1452-025, not a claim that the displayed automorphism is or is not generated by arbitrary polynomial LND exponentials.

## Scoped results

- Exact polynomial inverse and source-credited localized two-exponential factorization, with actual poles in the individual localized factors
- Genuine polynomial-flow words for relative parameter maps, bounded-degree coefficient closure, and exact finite-jet membership; no full-group closedness or uniform exact word inferred
- Free-product and polynomial-intersection results for the two localized directions, plus all-word degree exclusion for six specified polynomial Nagata-type flow directions, including ones moving x
- Arbitrary-affine word-form obstruction and an explicit allowed-subgroup example showing why degree growth is not a universal nonmembership invariant
- Finite algebraic systems that exactly certify arbitrary finite LND words; a positive factorization could use algebraic-number coefficients, but no target solution or uniform bound is obtained

The unrestricted three-variable finite-word membership question is the precise remaining gap. Factors moving x remain permitted.

## Independent review and checks

The separate full audit returned **PASS_SCOPED_PARTIALS**, with the original status still unsolved5/5. All five author outputs replay: 10,636 exact controls total, plus 1,741 fresh independent controls. Finite checks supplement the written proofs.

## Source credit and access

- Existing flexibility and finite-jet interpolation: [Arzhantsev et al., arXiv:1011.5375v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.5375v2), separated from exact full-automorphism membership

Reviewed sufficient-conditions result

This answers the sufficient-conditions request in OWR 9/2013, printed p. 492 (ID 30002291), with an explicit class of predictable pure-jump semimartingale drivers. The conclusion is joint finite-dimensional stable convergence of normalized quadratic variation, for every deterministic mesh tending to zero.

### Exact scope
- The jump measure is simple in time, with predictable compensator nu_s(dz) ds and a uniform deterministic bound on its quadratic rate integral z^2 nu_s(dz); the predictable drift is uniformly bounded. There is no Brownian component.
- The kernel is g(x)=x_+^alpha f(x), 0<alpha<1/2, with f continuously differentiable, f(0) nonzero, and exponential bounds on both f and f'.
- The full-past convolution is defined by an absolutely integrable drift term and an L2 compensated-jump term. The proof explicitly controls the prehistory singularity.
- The limit uses the squared jump sizes and independent uniform jump phases. The proof removes small-jump truncation by a uniform kernel-energy estimate.

No all-driver, maximal-hypothesis, functional-convergence, or historical novelty claim is made. The 2017 Lévy and 2018 Lévy-volatility results are credited and their stronger functional conclusions are kept within their own assumptions. Complete author preprints were inspected; the final Bernoulli full PDF was unavailable, and that access limitation is documented.

### Independent review and checks
The separate analytic/source review passed the unchanged proof, including stochastic Fubini, joint jump-time absolute continuity, stable phase mixing, truncation removal, and the exact source request.

Credited source correction
The original Lindskog–Boman contribution in **OWR10/2007, printed p.582** introduces the motivating question and immediately reports uniqueness under rapid decay or strict-cone support, together with unrestricted failure. It is not an unanswered demand for a universal necessary-and-sufficient classification.

Boman–Lindskog, **Support Theorems for the Radon Transform and Cramér–Wold Theorems**, J. Theor. Probab.22 (2009), 683–710, DOI10.1007/s10959-008-0151-0, gives the precise statements. Online publication was 18 March 2008. Full theorem/proof access here is the complete **arXiv:0802.4373v1** manuscript; the publisher's accessible page supplies metadata and abstract, not the subscription final PDF.

## Exact mathematical scope
The packet preserves signed locally finite measures on the **punctured space**, total-variation rather than cancellation assumptions, and halfspaces whose **closures avoid zero**. It credits three sufficient alternatives:
- Rapid total-variation decay at infinity, without a near-zero mass/moment bound
- Finite variation outside every origin ball and support in one **common closed cone Q whose nonzero points satisfy x·v>0 for a fixed vector v**
- A fixed nonintegral density-homogeneity degree below minus the dimension

The positive-measure data-homogeneity theorem is not extended to arbitrary signed measures. No origin atom is recovered and no exhaustive iff classification is asserted. The real part of the published z^(-3) counterexample has finite exterior total variation, infinite variation near zero, and zero allowed halfspace data; it is credited rather than claimed as new.

An independently reviewed classical-symmetry consequence resolves **5100064 / arXiv k905** on its natural quotient domain. The exact source is arXiv v11 Table 10 p.12: **inner caustic-contact polygon**, ordinary unit-circle vertex inversion about the **two original/shared foci**, signed straight-edge polygon areas, even primitive period. The published companion omits this row and the 900-series table.

For every strict nondegenerate confocal elliptical-caustic billiard of primitive even period, including primitive stars, the two inverse polygons have finite distinct vertices and **equal signed areas**. Their ratio is therefore **1 wherever the denominator is nonzero**. The proof credits classical central symmetry and asserts no novelty.

## Exact common-zero qualification
The primitive convex four-orbit on **x²/2+y²=1** has caustic axes squared 4/3 and 1/3. Its actual contact points are (±2√2/3, ±1/3). Focal inversion sends them to finite distinct collinear vertices on x=±1/2, so both signed areas are zero. The raw quotient is **0/0**, not a defined real value. A constant extension 1 is a separately labeled convention. This does not refute defined-locus invariance.

Both are admissible convex primitive four-orbits with strict nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustics:

- At **a²/b²=(1+sqrt(5))/2**, a required pair of perpendicular lines is distinct and parallel, so an antipedal vertex and its finite polygon area are undefined

Disposition
Unsolved after five substantive author turns. Separate adversarial review accepts the scoped partial packet; no optimal confining counterexample or universal automatic-convexity/A1 theorem is claimed.

## Exact source and remaining gap
The target is Bianchini–Zizza’s question in [OWR 52/2023, p. 2957](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/48173). Its short formulation leaves the global optimizer objective/quantifiers incomplete and prints A1 relative to vertical e2. The [later preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05324) uses horizontal e1 and proves an optimizer result within an already-convex class. Neither the weighted burned-area-plus-construction objective nor its terminal ray-length objective is silently replaced by prefix length minimization.

A full answer still needs an optimizer-specific global comparison preserving later construction and closing geometry, plus initial-tangent regularity. The original claim remains unresolved.

## Retained partials
- Explicit admissible nonconvex finite prefix
- Conditional radial and nonradial free-ray prefix length-convexity theorems, valid even with active budgets
- Causal first-contact prefix lemma and exact suffix budget accounting
- Exact planar counterexample to unchanged-suffix splicing: a shorter, locally admissible prefix advances a saturated continuation by the full length saving, making that fixed continuation inadmissible
- Strictly admissible Lipschitz prefix without an initial tangent or secant direction

The examples are nonconfining and are not asserted optimal. The splice counterexample refutes a proposed proof mechanism, not the OWR optimizer conjecture. Existing inputs are credited to Bianchini–Zizza, Zizza’s thesis, and [Bressan–Chiri](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00799); no novelty claim.

## Validation
The independent reviewer was uninvolved in the author route and explicitly audited the thin-wall route classification, involute level-set plateau, unchanged tangent contacts and negative terminal budget. All 23 frozen author-file hashes and four source hashes match; all five author outputs replay exactly (107, 102, 8,360, 158 and 366 controls). Nineteen additional independent identities/source checks pass. Finite diagnostics do not replace the analytic proofs or close the remaining optimizer gap.

## Exact source and credited result
This addresses **arXiv:2004.12497v11 Table 7 k609**, the focal **pedal areas of the inner caustic-contact polygon**, for even primitive billiard periods. The final companion Table 7 has no corresponding k609 row. Pedal vertices are projections onto inner-side supporting lines, not antipedal intersections or original/outer polygon feet.

The established Stachel central-symmetry theorem and elementary projection equivariance give equal signed areas, hence ratio **1 wherever defined**. This is a credited classical consequence with shared symmetry credit, not a new-discovery claim.

- For **convex primitive even orbits**, the denominator is always nonzero: a centrally symmetric strictly convex polygon has positive pedal signed area from every point in counterclockwise orientation
- For **primitive stars**, an exact winding-3 eight-orbit has common zero signed area with all projections finite. Its seventh-degree root certificate does not refute rational invariance; the raw 0/0 and its constant algebraic extension are distinguished

Exact result and credit
This draft supplies an independently reviewed classical-symmetry consequence for **5100024 / k406,a**, unchanged across arXiv v11 Table 5 p.7 and the published companion Table 5 p.348. It concerns the **outer tangent polygon's origin-antipedal**, not the original-orbit/focal centroid in k405/PR140. No novelty claim is made.

For every primitive even-period orbit with a strict nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, including primitive stars:
- All outer and antipedal vertices are finite
- The vertex centroid C0 is the ellipse center O
- The signed first-moment numerator is zero, so **C2=O wherever the signed area is nonzero**

## Genuine zero-area configurations
The raw signed-area centroid is undefined when its denominator vanishes. The proof analytically establishes that admissible finite even-period outer antipedals with zero signed area really occur, using an exact smooth-envelope area formula, a divided-difference limit with nonvanishing determinant, and fixed-period continuity. A constant extension O is explicitly optional and separate from the ordinary quotient. This is a domain qualification, not a refutation of the intended invariant.

[Proof](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/dot/math-5100024/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/5100024/PROOF.md), SHA-256 `6569729e6152ae1711f12ad88483af5e6346aa8d7b99dad234e49010e5c934d2`.

A separate reviewer passed the unchanged complete source-aware proof and zero-area construction, verified all nine author inputs and three primary PDFs, and supplied 16,506 independent exact controls plus 16,298 separately labeled high-precision diagnostics. Author replay is byte-identical. The review clarifies the edition-specific location of the centroid formula.

- Embedded triangulated spheres with coherent equal oriented face-area vectors, allowing coplanar adjacent triangles
- Maximal convex-face roof/dent example whose matching is not incidence preserving
- Embedded coherent sliding-cap example with two nonconvex polygonal faces; the parent-suggested mechanism is credited
- Rigidity for closed connected triangulated 2-manifolds with coherent correspondence and nonflat adjacency
- Coherent convex nonflat quadrilateral examples with explicit self-intersection

Unsolved after five substantive author turns. This draft preserves rigorously reviewed partial results and the exact remaining polynomial-bit comparison gap. It makes no hardness or novelty claim.

## Exact source
The original Neil Olver OWR question is comparison of sums of **(2/3)^r**, not the extracted 2^(r/3). The general bundle concerns rational-base sparse power sums with binary exponents and coefficient heights. The source page and all primary inputs were independently verified.

## Proved partials
- Polynomial-bit equality/zero testing via carries, with classical rational-root credit
- Explicit fixed-parameter sign algorithms and bounds in term count, not a full polynomial-bit algorithm
- Polynomial preprocessing of zero blocks and an adaptive certified sign procedure whose precision still depends on an uncontrolled margin
- Local root conditioning separated from rational-point separation
- Polynomial normalization into canonical positive rational-base carry words; efficient ordering remains unproved

See [RESULT.md](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/dot/math-30003999/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30003999/RESULT.md) for the scoped theorem list and exact gaps. All five author turn files are preserved.

## Independent review
A separate reviewer passed all frozen partial claims, reproduced all five author receipts byte-for-byte, verified all 29 author and six source hashes, and supplied 161,319 additional exact controls. Original target remains unresolved

Five substantive author turns were completed. No positive-probability stochastic percolation construction or lattice impossibility theorem was obtained, and the source's additional uniqueness question remains unanswered. The exact target retains d≥2, alpha>1, bounded strictly positive firing rates with infimum zero, and standard all-one initial tallies.

## Reviewed partial results

- A geometric and independent-thinning obstruction to directly transferring the regular-tree construction
- An explicit percolating deterministic alpha=2 equilibrium, attracting only within a relative support-face neighborhood
- A proof that the unit-start process never enters that relative neighborhood at finite time
- An l1 stochastic limiting-trajectory theorem for summable-square-root rate fields
- A continuous deterministic Lyapunov function and same-rate finite-component equilibria converging in l1 to the percolating equilibrium

The last result blocks an inference of percolation from l1 proximity. Deterministic support, face stability, stochastic compactness and random survival are kept distinct throughout.

## Independent validation

A separate full partial-package audit passed without mandatory correction. All17 frozen author hashes and two source PDFs matched; author4,300+132 exact receipts replayed byte-identically, and independent checks passed11,782 exact assertions. These support the written infinite-volume arguments and do not certify stochastic percolation. Classical source results are credited; no novelty or human-peer-review claim.

For random square-tiled surfaces in the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum, **first the square-count cutoff N tends to infinity, then genus g tends to infinity**. The full normalized horizontal-cylinder area multiset has an explicit asymptotic total-variation composition/Dirichlet model. At every mesoscopic scale s_g→0 with g s_g→infinity, the area process converges to PPP(dx/(2x)), with every fixed compact-window joint count moment converging.

In particular, the source's count in **[1/sqrt(g),2/sqrt(g)]** tends to **Poisson(log(2)/2)**; its mean and variance tend to log(2)/2, and its zero-count probability tends to 1/sqrt(2).

These are maximal horizontal cylinders, with the same vertical marginal by rotation. No joint horizontal/vertical independence, diagonal N(g) limit, other-stratum theorem, primitive-cover restriction, or all-directions count is asserted.

Overall disposition: unsolved, 5/5

The general finite-graph deterministic-limit question and the several-food modeling question remain unresolved after five substantive author turns. No excluded parallel-food Pólya example is presented as a counterexample to the intended conjecture.

## Independently reviewed partial results

- Exact killed-edge drift and rank-two formulas, and own-weight concavity
- A nonzero-curl obstruction to the natural gradient mechanism
- Almost-sure deterministic limits on every ordinary finite tree, including zero branches
- Almost-sure deterministic positive limits for any connected finite cyclic core rooted at the nest, with food attached by a fresh path of length at least two

The last proof separately establishes a unique positive equilibrium, global ODE attraction and stochastic persistence. It does not extend automatically to competing routes to food. The review clarifies the trivial edgeless core and stopped-coupling localization.

A secondary source-qualified consequence challenges only the paper's additional positivity sentence: the accessible pendant in N–a–F with pendant a–b has zero normalized limit despite nest–food distance two. The inspected source does not exclude such dangling edges; an intended additional restriction would change that assertion. This does not solve the imported deterministic-limit target and carries no novelty claim.

## Validation and queue

PASS_SCOPED_PARTIALS. All frozen author files remain unchanged; five independent review artifacts are included. Author exact checker: 1,073 assertions. Independent Fraction checker: 4,220 assertions. Sixty finite ODE runs remain explicitly inconclusive diagnostics.

Disposition
Unsolved after five substantive author turns. This draft preserves partial results and a separate adversarial review; it claims neither a positive identity relation lacking a pointed lift nor a universal lifting theorem.

## Exact target and remaining gap
Korkmaz's Question 13 in [OWR 56/2016, p. 3189](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46660) asks about prescribed positive twist factors lifted to one marked point. Independent choices of individual curve lifts are retained. The relative one-critical-point disk example is not an original-target counterexample. The actual Baykur–Hamada 48-factor genus-nine cap is homologically removable, but its complete based nonabelian words/actions and the universal smooth-extension problem remain uncertified.

## Preserved partials and credit
The five frozen turns develop the integral point-pushing lattice, a relative Heisenberg obstruction, a restricted positive-completion no-go, an ordered quotient criterion with nontrivial twist actions, and the concrete integral cap certificate. Inputs are credited to [Hillman–Pedrotti](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10943), [Smith](https://doi.org/10.2140/gt.1999.3.211), and [Baykur–Hamada](https://doi.org/10.4171/JEMS/1326). No novelty claim. A later seminar announcement with incomplete accessible hypotheses is not used as a theorem.

## Independent validation
Separate reviewer: PASS_PARTIAL_ORIGINAL_TARGET_UNSOLVED_5_OF_5. All 22 author-file hashes and six source hashes match; all four author outputs reproduce exactly. A distinct checker passes 1,102 exact controls. These diagnostics do not certify a global monodromy word.

The original frozen files retain their pre-review labels; the added independent_review/ records the final verdict. The review binds FROZEN_MANIFEST.json SHA256 1819b4437ed2fc5b8421654efb1daa45ed8de1ef3b103adccd6d3b89bdbd1452 and RESULT.md SHA256 9fac66080abf00bf01980e27edef2d61bffe56c08ece04893340af0a7f4bf276.

## Scope and access
Only the target's 32 portable author/review files and its single QUEUE.md row are changed. Source PDFs, extracted full texts, diagrams, complete imported record, and private notes are excluded. Source-aware paired result

This PR contains two independently reviewed results that must be read together:

1. Under geometric consistency (G), the diagonal-omitting cubic DDA is spectrally correct outside the exact static lattice interval: no pollution, convergence with algebraic multiplicities, and norm-convergent embedded Riesz projections. This covers all bounded Lipschitz and boundary-measure-zero particles.
2. The literal arbitrary-compact-support interpretation is false. At real frequency kappa = 1/10000, a positive-volume compact set with **empty interior**, supplemented by the **measure-zero sampling anchor {0}**, has an isolated nonreal continuum eigenvalue, although every h = 1/n DDA matrix is the 3-by-3 zero matrix.

The counterexample does **not** refute DDA for regular particles. The brief source does not state a technical domain assumption; the PR makes that ambiguity explicit rather than treating (G) as a printed hypothesis. The matrix approximates A_kappa minus I/3 throughout.

## Proofs and separate reviews

The first proof establishes static strong consistency and Hilbert–Schmidt convergence of the dynamic correction, then compact Fredholm/Riesz convergence. The second proves the ball's isolated static mode and a quantitative nonreal small-frequency perturbation, then preserves it under continuum mask convergence. No numerical eigenvalue is used in the counterexample.

Both independent audits are included unchanged. Author checks: 301 controls for the first proof, 482 exact scope controls for the second. Independent controls: 625 plus nonnormal diagnostics, and 748 exact scope controls. These are checks, not proof substitutes.

The static lattice theorem is credited to Costabel–Dauge–Nedaiasl; standard compact-operator theory is credited. No novelty or priority guarantee is made.

- An intrinsic trace criterion restricted to singular schemes admitting an everywhere-corank-one presentation

Result

Proves the exact arXiv k904,a signed-area product invariant for primitive odd elliptic-billiard periods, including stars. The vertices belong to the outer tangent polygon and inversion centers are the original billiard foci. The N=3 critical divisor cancellation is handled explicitly. Nondegenerate nested confocal ellipses are the stated scope.

## Review and reproducibility

A separate uninvolved adversarial reviewer passed the full source target and proof. The unchanged proof is bound by SHA-256 `9640ed4bc6c6b0b56f0235c0e28513e9c3ca94c53cb75d2cb2eecee5b45b075e`. Author checks: 102,770 exact assertions and 3,288 numerical diagnostics. Independent checks: 8,438 exact assertions and 5,412 separate 90-digit diagnostics. Only a source-navigation typo was corrected during review.

## Scope and provenance

The source is arXiv:2004.12497v11 Table 10; its published shorter companion omits the 900-series. Original-vertex inversion and inversion about the outer locus's own foci are different targets. Classical parametrization, Jacobi identities, and meromorphic methods are credited. No novelty or human-peer-review claim.

One substantive author turn produced the complete candidate. QUEUE.md changes only this problem's row to claimed_solved, 1/5. Exact result and source scope
Proves the phase invariance of the product of the two **signed focal-pedal areas of the outer tangent polygon** for every odd primitive elliptic-billiard period, including primitive star turning numbers, in a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal ellipse pair.

**Edition warning:** this is **k605,a in arXiv:2004.12497v11, Table 7, p. 9**, renamed **k606 in the published Table 7, p. 349**. Published k605 is the different original-orbit pedal product. The proof uses projections onto outer side lines, not the original billiard chords.

## Proof and independent review
The explicit focal foot map has two adjacent simple poles with collinear opposite residues. Their possible double-pole area coefficient cancels. Reflection and imaginary anti-periodicity on the reduced torus then force complementary half-period zeros; odd period makes exchanging foci exactly that half-period shift.

## Proof and attribution

A pointwise identity realizes the center-pedal polygon as a fixed linear image of a quarter-shifted edge-vector polygon. Both signed areas reduce to a cyclic Jacobi dn trace. Its effective order is odd exactly in the stated period range; reflected zeros cancel both possible pole sets, so the required trace product is constant on the compact torus.

Stachel's canonical parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and elementary polarity are credited inputs. Stachel, Journal of Geometry 112, article 40 (2021), Theorem 4.5, p. 24 explicitly proves k118: for odd-period elliptic billiards, both positive contact-segment sums equal the invariant perimeter divided by two. This is an already-published result, not a new proof or novelty claim.

The packet checks both invariant-table editions, the cyclic right-segment indexing shift, primitive odd stars with either turning-number parity, and repeated odd traversals. The separate review records a harmless printed perimeter-formula sign inconsistency; the invariant conclusion does not depend on it.

Result
Claimed full proof of k903,a for odd primitive periods, including permitted star traversals, in the strict nondegenerate confocal ellipse setting a > b > 0. The two polygons are obtained by unit-circle inversion of the ORIGINAL orbit vertices about the two ORIGINAL billiard foci. Their signed traversal-area product is constant.

The proof uses the classical genus-one Poncelet flag framework. Odd order separates the four common-tangent orbits; reversal lowers each focal area's apparent double poles to simple poles, while the opposite focal area vanishes there. The product is holomorphic on the compact flag curve. No conclusion from the separate k303,a target is assumed.

## Exact sources and credit
- [Reznik–Garcia–Koiller arXiv v11, Table 10 p. 12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.12497v11) is the exact k903,a source. The shorter published Fifty New Invariants companion has no k903 row.
- [The Talented Mr. Inversive Triangle](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.03020), Proposition 7 and Conjecture 1, credits the known N=3 case and states the general odd-period question.
- [Chavez-Caliz](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/020-0154.pdf), p. 98, supplies the classical flag-curve framework.
- The bicentric source DOI was corrected to [10.1007/s40598-021-00188-6](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40598-021-00188-6) and independently rechecked. No mathematical proof change was needed.

No novelty or priority claim.

## Independent review
Separate full-target PASS for unchanged candidate SHA-256 `c4c2c5399d46f8aa30c4580160ea15a1375939eab3a2ba390d74abdce9a30905`. Review SHA-256 `966d99ee9c85a31dcd87713a0838d42c4aadf47719a732ea90184e769439b1c5`.

Author controls: 91 exact assertions. Fresh independent controls: 3,553 exact assertions and 1,296 numerical diagnostics, including near-pole checks; author output replayed byte-for-byte. Numerical diagnostics are not interval certificates or the general proof.

## Scope and accounting
Only the target attempt folder and its QUEUE row change, to claimed_solved at substantive author 1/5. Frozen pre-review files and their hashes are retained; PUBLICATION.md and PUBLICATION_STATUS.json give the later assessment. Downloaded PDFs, full extracted texts, source renders and private context are excluded. The unit normalization, original vertex/focus identities, signed-area convention and primitive odd scope are explicit.

Outcome: original target unresolved after five substantive author turns

This draft preserves reviewed partial results for 30004757 / OWR-8415338-004. It does **not** solve the precise finite-separation tangent-cone and Hessian-asymptotics problem, including the general polyhedral/Y-shaped case. Queue disposition: **unsolved, 5/5**.

### Strongest reviewed partial result
A genuine source-type two-mass family with fixed isotropic quadratic and additive normalization has individual tangent bodies converging to half-balls as the masses collide, while the merged potential has a full-ball tangent body. A further normalization can hold both individual atom weights fixed. This proves noncommutation of these limits and excludes uniform C2,beta estimates across the degeneration; it does not refute or prove individual finite-separation smoothness.

The package also contains:
- a C1 description away from the inward ray in the axisymmetric two-mass case
- exact local and homogeneous obstacle models, explicitly not identified with the global source cone
- a localized flat-face restriction and a conditional angular/Hessian coefficient identity

### Independent review and reproducibility
The [independent review](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/0294c3bb00932830d69315c08b7ea09099c3ef29/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004757/independent_review/INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md) passes all frozen **partial** claims with the original target unsolved. Review SHA-256: c34f9e86ca6422ea578dd813a1a0e7c5b65bc0887583d7174f3be426f095f0d3.

All 19 frozen input files matched; all 40 author algebra checks replayed byte-for-byte; the independently authored checker passed 26 exact checks. These are algebra controls, not numerical PDE solutions. The original frozen manifest is retained unchanged; PUBLICATION_STATUS.md records the later review verdict.

### Source and credit
The target is the real Alexandrov problem in [OWR 35/2021, pp1884–1886](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46911), Problem4. Nonpolyhedral obstacles are the separate Problem5. The construction and barriers are credited to Mooney; related existence/stability results to Mooney–Rakshit; regularity and dimension inputs to Huang–Tang–Wang and Jin–Tu–Xiong. The model mechanism is Pogorelov-type. No novelty or priority is certified.

Result
Claimed full source-target proof of k303,a: for primitive elliptic-billiard period N congruent to 2 modulo 4 and every fixed real point M, the product of the outer tangent polygon’s signed area and its pedal’s signed area is constant. The setting is a strict nondegenerate confocal ellipse pair with a > b > 0. The pedal feet are taken to the outer tangent side lines, not the original billiard chords.

The proof establishes outer-pedal area B_M = c_M A using the two-simple-pole space on a genus-one flag quotient, then applies Chavez-Caliz’s published even-period AA′ theorem. Standard flag-curve and Riemann–Roch inputs are explicitly credited. No novelty or priority assertion.

Sources: [Reznik–Garcia–Koiller, arXiv v11, Table 4 p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.12497v11), [published companion, Table 4 p. 346](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/021-0174.pdf), and [Chavez-Caliz, Theorems 3/6](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/020-0154.pdf).

## Independent review
- Separate full-target PASS; no core mathematical correction required.
- Exact reviewed candidate SHA-256: `e48aa989fb9282d09fdf58e7e4f6eee78e757ff0686f4cc35dc691e21f3d1fd3`.
- Review SHA-256: `b1a3b3b00189c8e017267c6cb6728931f0199ed3f2e178067f831d17eeb01fe9`.
- 1,757 independent exact assertions and 26,568 high-precision numerical diagnostics pass; both author exact programs replay. Numerical controls are not interval certificates or the general proof.
- Pole completeness, quotient multiplicities, the odd-half-period congruence, double-pole cancellation, and reversal with M fixed were independently audited.

## Scope
Only the target attempt folder and its QUEUE row change, to claimed_solved at author 1/5. The published input is credited; nearby k203,a and odd-period k303,b are distinct targets. A scope-only v2 correction removes an extraneous circular-boundary aside; its history is retained. Downloaded copyrighted papers, full extracted texts, page renders and private context are excluded.

This is **credited existing mathematics, not a new discovery**.

The proof verifies complex transverse general position for every noncircular strictly nested confocal ellipse pair. Scope: **signed shoelace areas, even primitive period, nondegenerate elliptical caustic**, including star polygons. No hyperbolic/degenerate-caustic, repeated-odd-orbit, or unsigned-filled-region extension is claimed.

Result
Claimed full affirmative existence result for 30004690 / OWR-7155446-005: smooth strictly Kähler boundary data on P¹ × ∂D whose weak Bedford–Taylor HCMA solution fails to be twice differentiable at a point with 0 < |τ| < 1.

The construction credits Ross–Witt Nyström, *Applications of the duality between the Homogeneous Complex Monge–Ampère Equation and the Hele-Shaw flow*, AIF 69 (2019), 1–30, DOI [10.5802/aif.3237](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.3237.pdf). Their finite-time contact-arc construction is the input. The additional Green comparison and Legendre argument prove the interior defect; it is not inferred merely from boundary nonsmoothness or loss of rank. Original target: [OWR 25/2021, pp. 1321–1325](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46904). No novelty or priority claim.

## Review and evidence
- Separate adversarial full-target PASS, with published-source geometry, zero-area harmonic continuation, finite strictly negative pre-contact time curvature, and the interior twisting map independently checked.
- Unchanged candidate SHA-256: `85f04e81c5f02b1d867de50a82008c0d69ad2ecb962501ab2750a84ba473eed7`.
