- Independently authored scalar controls: 81 cases, 486 exact assertions. They check signs and conjugacy; the PDE result rests on the analytic proof.
- Full published PDF was recovered and read; source URLs, hashes and access history are recorded. Downloaded copyrighted papers and complete extracted texts are excluded.

## Scope and accounting
Only the target attempt folder and its QUEUE.md row change. Status is `claimed_solved`, with 4/5 documented recovered substantive turns. The historical interrupted count remains unknown and has not been reset. The full reviewed result permits stopping before turn 5. Earlier unsuccessful/conditional routes remain as historical author checkpoints and are not promoted as separately reviewed theorems. Frozen pre-review wording is retained; README and PUBLICATION_STATUS.json state the current assessment.

Reviewed result

This gives a negative result for the original **second-variable** generic-initial degree conjecture in characteristic zero. The essential central arrangement

`Q = x y (x-y) (x-2y) z w (x+z+w)`

has a minimal generic-initial generator of degree 7 involving the third variable, while the least pure power of the second variable has degree 8. The proof establishes generic-section ranks algebraically through polar syzygies and binary Hilbert-Burch. Exact rational computations are supplementary; genericity is not inferred from a sample.

## Source and scope

The imported first-variable threshold was a transcription error and is not counted as a discovery. The original corrected x2 conjecture, the published three-variable arrangement theorem, and the classical sectional-matrix methods are explicitly credited. This is a four-dimensional example; restricting its ambient Jacobian is not the same as taking the Jacobian of the restricted arrangement.

## Independent review and checks

Separate full adversarial AI review passed the unchanged frozen proof with no mathematical correction. The package includes the full review, exact input hashes, an independently authored standard-library verifier, and rational row-operation/minor certificates for all six Macaulay ranks. Author, independent, and additional edge-case controls reproduce exactly.

The result is AI-reviewed and unrefereed. No historical-priority, novelty, or smallest-counterexample claim is made. Historical interrupted author-turn usage remains unknown and nonzero; one documented recovered substantive turn produced the complete candidate. The queue preserves that distinction.

Only this problem's attempt folder and its single queue row change. No copyrighted primary-source PDFs, extracted article text, or source-page images are included.

This draft preserves a complete, independently AI-reviewed proof for the parity-aware type A0 interpretation of Fuchs's Conjecture 3.2. The proof uses the classical double-pentagon/virtual-Weierstrass framework, an edge-midpoint half-turn, and a short common-neighbor argument in the dodecahedral graph.

The source wording caveat is essential: the isolated beta-alpha=2pi/5 shortcut in the imported statement also admits the two direct pentagon diagonals, which have graph-distance-two endpoints. The literal extracted sentence is false. PROOF_V2.md states and proves the parity-aware theorem separately and identifies exactly these two exceptions. This draft must not be described as an affirmative proof of the unqualified shortcut.

## Independent checks

- Exact reviewed PROOF_V2.md SHA256: f96288e95c946731091989cea3eb087829c94cf966898dae792122567da3f16b
- Scope-matched independent AI review: independent_review/FINAL_REVIEW.md, PASS
- A separately written checker over Q[z]/Phi_5 reconstructs the public 16-face witness without importing its software or the author's checker
- The witness's geometry, all 15 crossings, first-vertex shortness, graph distance 2, and squared length (307+137sqrt(5))/2 pass
- Transported billiard labels and Figure 8 give beta-alpha=144 degrees and type A1 for that witness; the public 72-degree subtraction uses the other physical boundary ray and an interior angle
- Exact checks of all 30 edge-axis half-turns corroborate the proof; five local unit tests pass

All proof, source-scope caveats, exact code and output, original and final reviews, and hash receipts are under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/5000007/. Downloaded source PDFs and third-party software are not republished or executed.

## Limits and history

Disposition

Credited source correction and independent source/proof-validation hold for problem 30001704 (OWR-4798-031). This is not a new finiteness proof, a claim that the published theorem is false, or a claim of historical openness. The campaign QUEUE row is `unsolved`, 0/5 fresh proof-search approaches, with that evidence-level qualification explicit.

## Primary source and exact scope

Ed Swartz, *Face Enumeration on Manifolds*, Oberwolfach Report 24/2012, Theorem 7, printed p. 1429, explicitly announces bounded-complexity finiteness of PL-homeomorphism types. The report assumes connected manifolds; the complexity minimum is over simplicial-complex triangulations. Setting d=D+1 matches h2 minus the number of interior vertices with the invariant in the original 2011 question. The match is for the intended connected simplicial/PL interpretation, not an unqualified enlargement to disconnected or non-PL categories.

- [Original question, OWR 8/2011, p. 412](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46323)
- [Affirmative announcement, OWR 24/2012, pp. 1427–1429](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46393)
- [Swartz's earlier full author manuscript](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~ebs/Edges.pdf) proves the closed-manifold theorem only

## Independent validation

A separate source/scope review passes. An independently authored checker passes 1,248 exact assertions covering the dimension shift, cone-completion counts and links, stacking, disconnected/closed normalization controls, nonzero interior-vertex examples, and the recorded solid-torus examples with homology controls. These computations do not prove general topological finiteness.

All eight recorded source hashes were independently reproduced. Two source-manifest URLs were corrected to the MFO mirrors whose bytes match the preserved original hashes. The correction was separately rechecked and changes no mathematics or status.

## Access limits and file scope

The full supporting proof of the announced boundary theorem was not located or independently validated. Related later papers are not substituted for that proof. The assigned problem website was inaccessible in the original audit; the pinned complete source record is preserved.

Changes are limited to the 30001704 attempt package and its one QUEUE row. The package includes source provenance, review reports, independently authored diagnostic code and receipts. Downloaded papers, rendered source images, private coordination material, and environment-specific paths are excluded. An exact broken-Hessian moment criterion characterizes one extra integrated Gaussian-curvature order for all smooth graph jets on a shrinking patch. Odd rotational fans satisfy it without source-defined mirrored triangle pairs, and an exact degree-three diagnostic shows the parity limitation.

The original global mesh characterization remains **unsolved, 1/5**. A fixed-domain mesh family made from these fans is not constructed; the global weighted estimate is conditional. The July 2026 authors' preprint, earlier symmetric integration results, parametrization lifting and elementwise-curvature scope are explicitly credited and distinguished.

Separate adversarial review passed with no correction. All 3,745 submitted exact assertions reproduce byte-for-byte, and 4,971 independent controls pass, including interpolation and boundary-flux calculations over cyclotomic fields. Credited affirmative answer to Przytycki's higher-genus skein-torsion question

Belletti–Detcherry's 2024 preprint, published in IMRN in 2025, supplies manifolds with skein torsion but no essential spheres or tori, and stronger examples excluding any prescribed low-genus range. This resolves the literal existential Problem4.2 in Ohtsuki's list.

The package checks the original Z[A±1] coefficient ring and reconstructs the dimension-jump argument with explicit localization-kernel handling. Published generic finiteness and geometric existence are credited dependencies; finite computation does not certify those imported theorems. The full 2024 preprint was read; final journal full text was not compared.

Recommended status: already_solved, 0/5 new-discovery attempts. All 1,675 exact controls pass. Separate adversarial AI review passed for the unchanged artifact, with 9,803 independent controls. The full review and both checkers are included. No resolution of the adjacent universal conjecture, explicit torsion-link construction, or campaign-priority claim.

Problem 2.27 asks whether the finite-type invariants vanishing on the actual-link zeros of an arbitrary ideal always form its radical. This gives a nonempty-zero-set counterexample over C. Let g be the sum of squared pairwise linking numbers and I=(g(4g−1)). The actual zeros are exactly the algebraically split links, so g vanishes there; nevertheless g is not in the radical of I.

The obstruction is proved in the full finite-type invariant algebra. Restriction to the two-strand full-twist family is polynomial for every finite-type invariant, by the singular-link finite-difference relation. Evaluating that polynomial at one-half defines a character sending I to zero and g to 1/4. The proof does not rely on ideal membership in a polynomial subalgebra alone.

A separate adversarial source/proof review passed without corrections. All 8,460 submitted controls replay byte-identically; 20,980 independent controls pass. Complete fixed-dimensional closure as a credited consequence

For positive probability vectors x and y in the same fixed dimension d, the three weak power-sum conditions in the original OWR question characterize approximation of x by vectors x_k in that same dimension satisfying multiple-copy majorization against the unchanged y.

The proof imports Mu–Pomatto–Strack–Tamuz's published 2021 supplement, Proposition 8, with full attribution. Mixing nonuniform x slightly with the uniform vector supplies every strict positive/negative Rényi inequality, the derivative-at-zero inequality and the unequal extrema required by that theorem. The uniform case is handled directly. The approximation never adds coordinates or changes y.

This scoped package preserves the source's terminal L1 norm, equidistant observations and same scalar Brownian driver. It proves exact scaling and conditional-information formulas, computes a boundary-case finite-grid optimizer, and identifies the missing information in the usual mean-reversion time change.

The known rate theorems are credited. The source year and a misattributed arXiv citation are corrected. A relevant 2025 reflected-SDE theorem has an explicit full-text access hold; older endpoint estimates are not advertised as the best current bounds.

Exact result and source scope

This independently reviewed candidate answers the source's **existential growing-seed question**: for every unbounded finite-second-moment degree law supported on integers at least two, and every fixed positive rate disadvantage, a deterministic slowly diverging degree threshold can select seeds with vanishing vertex density and vanishing half-edge density while the slower infection captures 1-o_P(1) of vertices.

Seeds are selected using degrees before pairing or passage-time sampling. The faster infection starts uniformly within a fixed low-degree class. The proof uses a protected finite path, a joint fixed-time local exploration, and a justified deterministic diagonal schedule.

**Scope exclusions are essential:** no single-hub theorem, prescribed seed budget, sharp degree/rate threshold, or graph/weight-aware adversarial-root guarantee is claimed. The original OWR paragraph and supporting paper explicitly allow initial counts growing with n; the independent reviewer separately verified that source interpretation. Existing branching-exploration methods and random-regular growing-seed results are credited; historical priority is unestablished.

Recommended status: **claimed_solved, 2/5 approaches**, for the stated existential regime.

## Verification

The frozen proof is unchanged. All 11,561 author assertions reproduce byte-identically. Separate adversarial AI review passed, with 62,001 independent assertions over 9,999 finite weighted competitions; eight unchanged review files are included. Finite controls do not replace the asymptotic probability proof. No human peer-review claim.

Only this problem's research folder is changed. Queue status is coordinated separately.

Credited known affirmative resolution

Original OWR Problem 10 asks whether every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space supports a pair or larger finite tuple with one common vector whose same-time co-orbit is dense in the full product. Shkarin's published Theorem D supplies this result for every prescribed finite size, over either real or complex scalars, even on separable infinite-dimensional Fréchet spaces.

The package reconstructs the credited short similarity argument and explicitly records its pre-existing mixing/self-direct-sum input. It preserves Shkarin's attribution to earlier Bès–Martin–Peris and Salas constructions. This is a source/status correction, with no new-discovery claim.

## Independent review

- PASS_COMPLETE_CREDITED_KNOWN_EXISTENCE_RESULT, no corrections
- Frozen mathematical artifact: 04a12c724f2c57717465e856f58c79012b921e8b800cf3e8f8abc388f14503db
- Independent review: ecf03aabf0c5babc05829006e408f238700af0c011df6006237e6abd5ab36bd6
- 32,184 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically; 3,650 independent controls pass over Q and Q(i)
- Recommendation: already_solved 0/5; one source/proof validation family recorded separately

Finite-dimensional test matrices verify transporter and orbit identities; they are not hypercyclic witnesses. The frozen manuscript's historical pending-review line is superseded by the completed review and current README/status. This package has not undergone human peer review.

## Exact scope and sources

No extra commutativity, dense set of starting vectors, or separable-dual hypothesis is imposed. The dual theorem and stronger disjoint-mixing/transitivity questions are separate. The complete primary author manuscript and the relevant published Grivaux input were read; the final typeset Shkarin PDF was inaccessible. Journal publication is 2010, while the arXiv deposit is 2012.

All changes are isolated under attempts/30000567. Parent coordination will update the queue. One draft PR; no merge or release.

Scoped p-subgroup result for the Ellers–Murray block problem

The unrestricted symmetric-subgroup conjecture remains unsolved after two approaches. The package proves a finite-p-group fixed-algebra theorem, yielding the exact desired block description for l=2 in characteristic two for every n. It includes an explicit non-p-group control identifying why the method does not prove the general case.

The source's natural subgroup embedding and primitive-central convention are preserved. Prior small-gap cases, the current Fayers–Putignano ribbon/belt theorem, and the out-of-scope S6/A4 counterexample are credited. No historical-priority claim is made.

All 147 exact standard-library controls pass. Separate adversarial AI review passed for the unchanged frozen proof, with 121 independent controls. The full report and both reproducible checkers are included. Recommended status: unsolved, 2/5; parent owns the queue row. No human-peer-review or full-resolution claim.

Complete counterexample at a fixed nonboundary rank

For the stationary binary Markov source with transition matrix ((3/4,1/4),(1/4,3/4)), the proof specifies one fixed rank proportion whose source coding has 1s at square positions. This rank is a continuity point of the first-order cost profile and is not a cylinder boundary.

Along an explicit deterministic sample-size subsequence, two positive-probability cost bands separate by much more than sqrt(n). Therefore the one-dimensional radix-selection cost is not tight under sqrt(n) scaling for **any deterministic centering**, including expectation centering. This gives a negative answer to universal fixed-rank marginal convergence in the original source model.

## Independent validation

- Separate adversarial review: PASS_COMPLETE_NONBOUNDARY_COUNTEREXAMPLE, no corrections
- Frozen proof SHA-256: c72a38099e93b4d593be231e8f0c4ad726a399c3d61283da9f7b1f7e55801a5c
- Review SHA-256: e3aa05eac01c81d82b869f206930fc70da1b73c205416c22ceec26ee6908263c
- 16,642 submitted exact controls reproduce byte-for-byte; 44,602 independent controls pass
- One substantive route, gpt-6-astra at xhigh; recommendation claimed_solved 1/5

The proof uses an elementary uniform cost bound and the binomial quantile CLT; finite controls support its identities rather than replace the asymptotic argument. The frozen manuscript's historical pending-review header is superseded by the completed review and current README/status.

## Scope and attribution

The later Leckey–Neininger–Sulzbach paper already proves a dense boundary-rank obstruction; that result is credited. Its subsequent open-marginal sentence creates a source-scope tension retained in the audit. This construction addresses a nonboundary continuity rank instead. No almost-everywhere rank classification, claim about random centering, historical-priority claim, or human peer-review claim is made. Full original and author manuscripts were read; final publisher-typeset comparison was unavailable.

Source-aware disposition

This audit treats OWR-14221-005 (30003069) as **already solved, 1/5 diagnostic approach**, for the authors' corrected all-complement rectangle-seed formulation. The equivalence is credited to Fang–Fourier (2018), with the positive-integer tensor-power normalization made explicit.

The rendered 2016 conjecture concerns barred G₀. Its frozen-label display has a mixed-cardinality typing defect away from n=2k. The later paper complements all labels and identifies the dual rectangle seed. Both the original defect and the imported missing-bar/unchanged-non-mirror misreading remain prominent. A 14-versus-15 facet check at Gr(3,6) diagnoses why the unchanged rectangle interpretation is false; it is not a counterexample to the barred-graph conjecture.

## Validation

The frozen mathematical artifact is unchanged. Separate adversarial AI source/mathematical review passed. All 9,642 author controls replay byte-identically; 42,438 independent exact controls include 826 rational facet witnesses. Eight unchanged review files are included.

This package credits the published general theorem rather than claiming a new flow proof, all-seed result, historical priority, or human peer review. Only this problem's folder is changed. Queue status is coordinated separately.

original OWR question asks for the order of the force-induced transition in the fully flexible partially directed polymer pulled horizontally. Owczarek–Prellberg (2007) and Brak et al. (2009) already cover this exact model: the transition is continuous and second order, with a 3/2 singularity in the limiting log-partition free energy.

This source-status package matches the walk, contact and ensemble conventions; proves the endpoint-reversal correspondence; records the critical curve and opposite free-energy sign conventions; and distinguishes the published limiting asymptotic from speculative finite-size expressions. Transverse force, stiffness and unrestricted walks remain outside this result. It makes no discovery claim or independent reproof of the published asymptotic machinery.

A separate adversarial source review passed without corrections. All 13,347 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically and 7,495 independent controls pass. These checks validate model correspondence and normalization, not the critical exponent. The eight-file review bundle and exact replay dependencies are included. original question asks whether noncomputable K-trivial oracles preserve ordinary logical depth or make its class strictly smaller. This package leaves that classification unresolved (2/5 approaches).

It proves a truth-table transfer lemma and uses Nies's published c.e. covering theorem to reduce universal equality, or existence of strictness, to c.e. K-trivial oracles. It also identifies a uniform output-preserving compiler obstruction, while explicitly distinguishing that stronger mechanism from the unresolved nonuniform complexity comparison. No noncomputable-oracle outcome or novelty claim is made.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without mandatory corrections. All 6,534 author controls reproduce byte-identically and 6,200 independent bounded controls pass. They compute no genuine Kolmogorov complexity and decide no infinite depth property.

Recommended queue status: unsolved, 2/5. Only the isolated research package and its review are included.

**Already solved by a published-theorem consequence; one reduction approach logged.** The focal-angle invariant k120 follows from Roitman–Garcia–Reznik’s 2021 bicentric cosine-sum theorem. This package provides a complete source audit and explicit coordinate/ordinary-angle bridge: focal polarity sends the fixed nested confocal ellipse pair to nested circles, and each original focal cosine is minus the internal-angle cosine of the polar polygon.

The scope includes simple and star Poncelet orbits in the original nondegenerate confocal-ellipse setting, with no parity restriction. The independent review explicitly checks the published Jacobi step/winding convention by a doubled traversal. This is credited existing mathematics, with no new-discovery claim or unsupported hyperbolic-caustic extension.

The proof checks the source's original-orbit half angles and outer tangent polygon, provides a continuous T²=−id family connecting the examples, and verifies common caustic, physical reflection and all nonzero denominators. Signed and ordinary areas coincide because both examples are convex and counterclockwise.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. The frozen proof is unchanged. All 10,073 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically; 8,397 independent rational/symbolic controls pass. Eight review files are included.

Two substantive approach families are recorded (2/5). This resolves the printed assertion by counterexample. original question asks for cohomological Brauer groups of arbitrary tame stacky curves, including non-DM and generic inertia. This package proves a formula under a dense schematic-open hypothesis and gives explicit generic-gerbe diagnostics; the general target remains unresolved (3/5 approaches).

The partial results include the local Schur-multiplier formula, two stacks with identical coarse curve and stabilizers but different Brauer groups, and an Artin–Schreier calculation for A¹ × Bμ_p in characteristic p. Imported structural theorems and their narrower hypotheses are credited; no general Azumaya comparison or novelty claim is made.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without mandatory corrections. All 77,458 submitted assertions replay byte-identically and 40,882 independent exact controls pass. These controls supplement the mathematical/source audit and do not prove the remaining arbitrary generic-inertia case.

Recommended queue status: unsolved, 3/5. This draft contains only the isolated research package and its review.

A positive-mutation strict-condensation example contradicts the source’s printed rate-one expression in that physical clock.

The existence and shape of a corrected profile remain unresolved. Complete analytic joint law, in explicit-transform form

Gives the finite-k joint Laplace transform of the Brownian first-visit cell lengths for both starting-position models in the full original source: independent uniform seeds and equidistant seeds. Every coefficient is a finite sum of deterministic finite-dimensional integrals of explicit one-dimensional exit kernels, over linear inequalities comparing cumulative physical hitting times. A uniform factorial bound controls truncation of the outer series, and compact-support moment determinacy identifies the full joint probability measure.

The walkers continue independently through previous targets, other starting points and encounters. The proof treats the singleton-target two-endpoint kernel and the spatial null sets of ties and repeated queries explicitly.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. The proof is unchanged from the reviewed snapshot. All 8,520 submitted exact controls reproduce byte-identically, and 46,056 independent controls pass. Eight independent review files are included.

This answers the distribution request in the stated explicit-transform sense. It does not claim a simple named density, efficient numerical quadrature, historical priority, or human peer review. The classical Brownian kernels and strong Markov property are credited. One substantive approach family is recorded (1/5). The coordinating task owns the claimed_solved queue update.

Credited known resolution

Provides a complete O(n²/log(2+n)) real-RAM algorithm for the exact original all-count interval problem, by reconstructing the established min-plus-convolution method of Bremner et al. (ESA 2006; Algorithmica 2014). Interval witnesses, repeated coordinates, and infeasible exact counts are handled explicitly.

The implementation's recursive generator was corrected during adversarial review to use one shared output list, so reporting costs O(P). The final proof and corrected implementation passed separate adversarial AI review: 10,388 submitted assertions and 22,962 independent exact controls. Nine review files are included.

One validation/reconstruction family is retained in the historical log; there are zero new-discovery attempts. The appropriate result status is already_solved. The coordinating task will update the queue separately.

This is an o(n²) arithmetic/comparison bound on the real RAM. It makes no O(n^(2−epsilon)) claim, bit-complexity speedup, lower-bound claim, or novelty claim. Full primary author versions were checked; the final journal-layout PDF was not compared. AI-reviewed research draft, not human peer reviewed.

Reviewed partial scope for KP-3.32; general target unresolved

This package repairs the source link and records the exact locally flat PL, based-ambient conventions. It derives a higher-genus small-I-bundle subclass directly from Baroni’s published boundary-trace and handlebody-extension algorithms, with full attribution.

The remaining gluing requirement is stated as a trace-subgroup compatibility problem. Exact examples show why forgetting the point at infinity, or treating noncommuting paired twists as a fixed multitwist vector, would be invalid shortcuts. Neither is a counterexample to decidability.

The original remains unsolved,1/5. There is no novelty claim and no general-genus algorithm. All 4,238 finite algebra controls pass and replay byte-identically. A separate adversarial AI review passed the scoped result without correction, with 55,932 independent exact controls. Its complete eight-file bundle is included and the mathematical snapshot is unchanged. This is not human peer review. The parent maintains the queue.

Complete sufficient-condition candidate

For every real alpha, define a=|1−alpha|, b=|alpha| and k=(a+2b−1+sqrt((a+2b−1)^2+8b))/4. The condition

Σ n[1+k(n−1)] |a_n| ≤ 1

implies membership in Miller's alpha-convex class. It guarantees zero avoidance and strict positivity inside the unit disk, including the equality budget. At alpha=0 and 1 it recovers the source's n and n² coefficient weights exactly.

For 0<alpha≤1, the interpolation parameter is sharp within this specific one-parameter weight family. No optimality for other weights or outside that range is claimed. The established two-denominator estimate and majorization method are credited, especially Kumar–Ravichandran (2017); priority is unestablished.

The exact AIM Problem22 has a counterexample already implied by Gritzmann–Langfeld–Wiegelmann, SIAM J. Discrete Math.25(2011), Remark2.3. This package supplies a self-contained sixteen-point certificate for the published rotated square and the exact four forms x, y, 2x+y and −x+2y.

The certificate also gives an explicit degree-eight convex body with real-analytic boundary and everywhere positive curvature. Its strict sign margins exclude a ridge-threshold representation even modulo planar null sets for arbitrary measurable finite-valued profiles, with no continuity or integrability assumption. A concrete patch-swapped nonconvex set has identical four continuous X-rays.

Recommended status: **already_solved, 1/5 validation/certificate families**. The square nonadditivity is expressly credited to2011. Historical priority of the explicit smooth/a.e. corollaries is unestablished, and no novelty claim is made. The imported dataset's previous special cases are retained as prior work. The separately numbered Problem23 about slabs is excluded.

Scoped partial result; original request unresolved

Penner's Problem 2 asks for a more closed-form component-count expression in Dehn–Thurston or other coordinates. This package gives an exact expanded permutation/kernel/determinant identity, including the boundary-arc correction, and identifies its possible exponential growth relative to binary input weights. It does not supply the requested tractable compressed expression.

The closed-case matching formula and existing polynomial-bit algorithms are credited. Narrow global-gcd and continuous-homogeneous obstructions are proved without claiming impossibility for every formula class. The complete 2025 Yaguchi–Yamamoto paper was unavailable, so current open status is not globally certified.

- Separate adversarial AI review: PASS_SCOPED_EXPANDED_FORMULA_AND_ARITHMETIC_OBSTRUCTIONS
- 7,775 author assertions replay byte-identically
- 10,900 independent union-find/Burnside and arithmetic controls pass
- Exact frozen artifact and complete review included

Bounded circle-free-body attempt; original unresolved

The exact source concerns escape of fixed-radius rigid circular rings, with boundary contact allowed. This package proves a clearance-level reformulation and necessary geometry for a hypothetical ring holding K+B: its plane must cut the core K, and the concentric ring with radius reduced by the ball radius is attached to K.

The missing step is a positive-clearance escape theorem. An exact ball example shows that enlarging an arbitrary escape path's ring radius does not supply that theorem, even though both diagnostic bodies are circle-free. It is explicitly not a counterexample to the original question. A separate lemma certifies small thickenings for an already supplied strictly positive-clearance path.

The known planar-set-plus-ball subclass is credited. A second, critical-pyramid route did not produce a certified counterexample. The original remains unsolved, 2/5, with no novelty claim. All 241 exact controls pass and replay byte-identically. The separate adversarial AI review passed the scoped statements with no mandatory corrections; its 711 independent exact controls also pass. The complete eight-file review bundle is included, and the mathematical snapshot is unchanged. This is not human peer review. The parent maintains the queue.

For every n >= 4, the Waring-polynomial candidate cannot be the single-state first-return-time generating function of any reversible countable-state Markov chain. For every n >= 2, the candidate is nonrational and cannot be an ordinary hitting-time generating function of a time-homogeneous finite-state chain. If it is a probability law, its mean is infinite.

The original target remains **unsolved, 2/5 substantive approaches**. These exclusions do not disprove coefficient positivity and do not exclude nonreversible chains or other random variables. Fill and Sokal's earlier small-n interpretations and recorded birth-and-death limitation are credited. No novelty claim.

**Unsolved, 3/5 approaches.** The original all-measure simultaneous-merger conjecture is not resolved.

This scoped package proves a four-sample necessary identity, so a fixed genuinely simultaneous coalescent has at most one candidate positive mutation rate for regeneration. A valid two-atom model passes that test and fails at sample size five, explicitly demonstrating the insufficiency. A separate all-sample argument excludes bounded-parent full-replacement models with no Kingman component.

The statement concerns any sampling-consistent regenerative ordering of the allelic partition, not only chronological freezing order. The known non-simultaneous Lambda classification and classical representation/recursion inputs are credited. There is no novelty or general Xi classification claim.

Reviewed affine comparison; broader original target unresolved

The primary OWR question compares Bernoulli preferential attachment with an adapted model having i.i.d. Poisson outdegrees and indegree-only attachment. The dataset's fixed-outdegree equality is a different, false assertion.

This package proves a comparison theorem for affine f(k)=ak+b, 0<=a<1 and 0<b<=1, with Poisson mean b/(1-a). It covers frozen and sequentially updated weights, zero outdegrees, alternative fixed finite seeds, and empirical local convergence in probability. The argument couples edge multiplicities with sublinear expected discrepancy, proves a degree-moment bound and transfers it to fixed-radius neighborhoods. A separate column-pruning concentration argument addresses the empirical convergence requirement.

The common Gamma–Poisson tree is a reformulation of Dereich–Mörters' credited Bernoulli limit. The current March 2026 universality paper's total-degree theorem is not substituted. General nonlinear concave functions, arbitrary unspecified adaptations and a no-parallel-edge convention are outside the theorem. The larger nonlinear interpretation remains unresolved.

A separate adversarial AI review passed the frozen theorem with no mandatory correction. All 35,349 submitted exact diagnostics replay byte-identically, and 98,943 independent exact controls pass. The eight review files are included unchanged. Priority is unestablished; no new-discovery or human-peer-review claim is made. Recommended queue status is unsolved, 1/5, because the general concave-rule target remains open here. The parent maintains the queue.

Credited classical consequence and literal-source correction

For the independent undirected inverse-square model in OWR Problem 2, the infinite cluster is one-ended whenever it exists. The proof combines Aizenman–Kesten–Newman's classical uniqueness theorem with an explicit positive-probability finite-set isolation argument. It handles the infinitely many potential incident edges using summability.

A precisely defined nearest-neighbor-parameter family has a critical point strictly between zero and one and positive critical density, using Newman–Schulman's existence theorem, Aizenman–Newman's density bound and a written right-continuity argument. Thus neither proposed ordinary graph-end count holds, and the critical conclusion is nonvacuous.

The package credits all classical results, preserves the ordinary-end interpretation and does not infer the speaker's intended alternative question. It makes no novelty claim. The full original contribution and all three primary journal-paper PDFs were retrieved; the deep imported theorems are distinguished from the elementary deduction audited here.

A separate adversarial AI review passed the frozen argument with no mandatory corrections. All 1,002 submitted exact finite diagnostics replay byte-identically, and 2,303 independent controls pass. The eight review files are included unchanged. The parent maintains the queue; recommended status is already_solved, 0/5.

Complete hardness proof
The exact fixed-root, destination-dependent path-cost arborescence problem is strongly NP-hard. The reduction from 3SAT uses a simple depth-three DAG, nonroot indegree at most three, and binary nonnegative costs. Every vertex is root-reachable. The optimum is exactly the minimum number of unsatisfied clauses.

A constant objective offset also gives hardness with strictly positive costs in {1,2}. The proof covers every feasible arborescence, not only trees selected by the reduction.

## Independent adversarial validation
- PASS_COMPLETE_STRONG_NP_HARDNESS_PROOF, with no corrections
- 57,135 submitted assertions replay byte-identically on 449 formulas and 12,696 arborescences
- Independent unfiltered enumeration checked 222,114 edge subsets across 114 formulas, including 1,674 actual arborescences; 14,397 assertions passed
- Frozen proof and eight independent-review files are included unchanged
- The exact original OWR Problem2 and the classical 3SAT source were checked

Record 30003998 duplicates this target and receives no separate attempt or PR. The distinct all-roots Problem1 / 30003996 uses a related literal-selection mechanism; that shared idea is credited rather than presented as an unrelated discovery. Historical priority remains unestablished, and the work has not undergone human peer review.

See unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30003997/README.md and PROOF.md. The proof's submission-time pending header is superseded by the completed review and release metadata. One proof family was used. The coordinating task owns queue updates.

Analytic necessary-and-sufficient parameter criterion
This gives an explicit integral condition in a,b,c for null-chain closure on the Minkowski ellipsoid. A global conformal-cylinder coordinate and a contour period identity compute the previously unnamed return-map translation. The criterion also proves a unique positive c for every prescribed positive rational winding ratio and gives an elementary formula when a=b.

The precise count matters: the GKT equator-return map has the displayed period criterion; a literal chain of full tropic-to-tropic arcs additionally requires **an even number of arcs**. Least periods and iterated closures are stated separately.

## Independent review and scope
- Separate adversarial geometry/source review: PASS_COMPLETE_ANALYTIC_CRITERION for the literal parameter-condition request
- 2,087 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically; 752 independent exact diagnostics pass
- The theorem and eight independent-review files are unchanged from the reviewed snapshots
- GKT's classical invariant-density and Poncelet results are credited
- This is an analytic criterion; no algebraic Cayley determinant or ordinary elliptic-torsion characterization is claimed
- The imported torsion shortcut is corrected by an explicit third-kind pole/residue computation
- Historical priority is unconfirmed, and there has been no human peer review

See unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/600008/README.md and ANALYTIC_CRITERION.md. The frozen theorem's submission-time header is superseded by the completed review and release metadata. One substantive approach was used; the coordinating task owns the claimed_solved queue update.

Result and scope

The original minimal-surface realization problem remains **unsolved, 2/5 approaches**.

This package restores the exact three-dimensional, minimal-genus, unknotted-thickening question and credits Dye's nonzero-homology result. It proves a conditional compression-circle test using Gabai's existing solid-torus surgery theorem: if the specified opposite-side compression circle is nonsplit from an unknot realization, every nonzero full twist gives a nontrivial classical realization without increasing supporting genus.

The universal existence of that nonsplit circle is **not proved**. Ambient splitting disks cannot simply be relocated into the thickened-surface complement, and first homology cannot supply that missing geometric step. No general realization theorem or counterexample is claimed.

## Independent verification

- Separate adversarial review: **PASS_SCOPED_PARTIAL_RESULTS**, no mandatory correction
- **2,121** author exact assertions reproduce byte-identically
- **724** independent exact diagnostics pass
- Compatible handlebody markings, zero winding, surgery slope, minimal-genus preservation and the remaining disk-location gap were separately audited
- Frozen proof SHA-256: `3f7cd405177c44d8d26064f6643d8847a9ecd86c17db22b32c1b024ac3292345`

The complete review and reproducible controls are included. Gabai's exact corollary and proof were read in indexed primary text; the local full-PDF and screenshot access limitation is explicitly retained. The algebraic controls do not decide splitting or certify geometric realization. No novelty or human peer review is claimed.

This package gives a complete affirmative proof in the closed oriented source setting: the constant pencil ω+sα remains contact, approaches the taut foliation, and transfers tightness through a finite smooth Gray path. An explicit smoothing argument treats C¹ forms without assuming a smooth foliation or a low-regularity Gray theorem.

The exact frozen proof passed a separate adversarial AI review with no mandatory correction. All 87 author controls replay byte-identically, and 89 independent exact diagnostics pass. The review and self-contained replay artifacts are included. The proof retains its original pending-review header solely to preserve the reviewed bytes; README and readiness record the final PASS.

A conditional C¹ sensitivity estimate states the missing derivative hypotheses. The source audit distinguishes mechanical symplecticity, cotangent-lift identities, and actual adjoint convergence, and credits the applicable 2015, 2024 and 2026 results. The control embedding is deliberately unactuated; no primal-control failure or novelty is claimed.

A separate adversarial AI review passed after adding the explicit initial-data assumption to the sufficient estimate. All 3,310 submitted and 1,118 independent symbolic/rational controls pass. The full review and reproducible snapshots are included. This has not undergone human peer review.

Scope and result

The original Lyapunov-function problem remains **unsolved, 2/5 approaches**. This package proves a scoped obstruction to the source's displayed, bounded time-independent δ,F functional family for one smooth nonnegative face-damping profile. The test uses compatible smooth initial pressure data supported inside the layer with zero auxiliary fields.

The quantification over the whole parameter family is handled by a high-frequency test forcing δ=s, followed by an exact positive-energy-derivative witness and an H¹ approximation to smooth compact data. A symmetric first-order formulation establishes the required local solution independently of the disputed energy estimate.

This does **not** establish PDE instability, rule out all Lyapunov functions, or settle the physical-region-only initial-data class. The original source and later energy literature already identify the variable-profile remainder; that work is explicitly credited, with no novelty claim.

## Evidence

- Full scoped proof, restored source equations, primary-literature audit and exact remaining gap
- Separate adversarial AI review: **PASS_SCOPED_FUNCTIONAL_OBSTRUCTION**, with no mandatory correction
- All **9,539** submitted exact assertions reproduce byte-identically
- **21** independent symbolic controls pass; the analytic limit, approximation and PDE-existence steps are separately audited in prose
- The proof is preserved at reviewed SHA-256 `b270af773ded6be5f0c6a1d6c8bfa942ac1fb726b163cb0e7eaa621fa427f8fe`

Review files and controls are included in the problem folder. This is an open draft for further review, not human peer review. No general stability or optimality claim is made.

Complete classification
This gives the point spectrum and full Banach-operator spectrum of f ↦ f∘A on complex C(U), with the supremum norm, for U the closed unit ball of an arbitrary complex norm and ||A||≤1. The statement covers zero and nilpotent eigenvalues, nonzero strictly stable eigenvalues, and peripheral eigenvalues in every combination.

The key step shows that every unimodular eigenfunction factors through the peripheral spectral projection, which is itself a contractive norm limit of powers of A. The resulting reversible-ball calculation and stable/nilpotent decomposition close the mixed-case reverse inclusion explicitly left open in Küster's 2015 thesis. Previously known cases, including its nilpotent-only Proposition 3.1.7, are credited. Historical priority of the completed classification remains unconfirmed.

Result and scope
The original marked-lifting problem remains **unsolved after two substantive approaches**. This package proves scoped geometric facts for the exact eight-line pentagon arrangement: the specified order-four incidence permutation has no affine or projective self-realization, while its square has a based, positive-meridian complex-linear realization and therefore the corresponding integral homotopy-compatible transfer action.

The excluded linear realization does not exclude an arbitrary topological, fundamental-group, or integral E-infinity lift. An unmarked Galois-complement equivalence also does not supply the prescribed marking. Published prior results are credited; no novelty claim is made.

## Validation
- Separate adversarial AI review: PASS for the scoped geometry and unresolved marked-lifting gap
- 111 exact submitted geometry controls and 703 independent controls pass
- Nine independent-review files, including the final status-only hash addendum and frozen checker dependencies, are included
- A separate exploratory screen of 24 truncated formal Magnus systems is explicitly uncertified as a fundamental-group calculation and supports no positive lifting claim

See unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30002203/README.md and OBSTRUCTION.md. The writeup has not undergone human peer review. The coordinating task updates the queue row separately.

Result

Complete counterexample to Krener's negative-curvature observability conjecture in its original smooth-manifold formulation.

Take a connected double cover of a closed hyperbolic surface, observe it through the covering projection followed by a smooth Nash isometric embedding into R17, and use zero dynamics. The exact finite-time observability Gramian is the pulled-back hyperbolic metric: complete, uniformly bounded and positive definite, with curvature −1 at T=1. Each attained output history has exactly two initial states.

The source allows a general state manifold and does not require simple connectivity or nonzero dynamics. The package includes both intrinsic uniform bounds and explicit finite-atlas bounds. It does not claim a stronger result for a separately restricted Euclidean state domain.

The full AND-layer average-maximal-sensitivity question remains **unsolved after two approaches**, including the source's weaker subpolynomial version.

## Scoped deductions
The statistic is the uniform expectation of the pointwise maximum. The package proves the logarithmic-fan-in special case, a fan-in-independent single-output bound, and a disjoint-block example showing a logarithmic loss is necessary for constant input ams.

A classical Hamming-syndrome construction disproves a proposed generic transfer from zero-side sensitivity to full sensitivity. It is **not a counterexample to the source**: the displayed conjunction representation has linear input ams. The common low-ams factorization remains the essential unresolved condition.

Graph-case theorem; original higher-dimensional target unresolved

This package proves Knudson's persistence-pairing realization conjecture for all finite graphs. It preserves the labeled pairs by postponing dying components, makes incident pairs consecutive, and then constructs the required descending integer function and generated-subcomplex filtration.

- Preserves the exact source function and tie-refinement conventions
- Includes implementation and 8,852 exact checks across 467 graph filtrations
- Clearly distinguishes Alec's prior 30000990/Conjecture2 counterexample; no old files are changed
- Records the higher-dimensional gap and the weaker scope of the finite order exploration
- No novelty or human-peer-review claim; original status remains unsolved, 2/5

Separate adversarial AI review passed on the unchanged frozen snapshot. The independent audit checked 93,948 graph filtrations, 252,878 single-pair postponements, and 2,073,304 exact assertions, including actual generated subcomplexes and labeled pairs. Its seven publication files are included unchanged. The original higher-dimensional conjecture remains unresolved. Parent owns the queue update.

Result and exact scope
An affirmative answer to OWR-785-003 in its asymptotic unitary-encoding model: the four-qubit W state is LOCC dense-codeable. Two independent senders can achieve rates 9/8 bits each per resource copy, totaling 9/4 bits for two transmitted qubits. The proof gives the stronger sum-rate supremum lower bound 3/2 + h₂(1/4) ≈ 2.311278.

Each sender sends her own qubit to her designated receiver. B1 Bell-measures the received pair and sends only the classical outcome to B2. B2's quantum block decoder is entirely local. Winter's established cq multiple-access direct theorem supplies independent-message codes with vanishing **average** error. There is no global quantum operation between receivers.

For a free strict 2-category, any nontrivial bubble forces an infinite cyclic subgroup in every positive even degree of its Street-nerve homology. This prevents agreement with polygraphic homology, which vanishes above degree 2. The proof combines Guetta's generator weights with Ara's natural B²N→K(Z,2) theorem.

- Establishes the necessary direction only
- Preserves the canonical comparison direction and all-composite-cell definition of a bubble
- Does not assume the separate degree 2 comparison conjecture or the bubble-free converse
- Includes 297 exact formal checks and complete source-scope/provenance notes
- No novelty or human-peer-review claim; proposed unsolved, 1/5

Separate adversarial AI review passed on the unchanged frozen snapshot. All 297 author controls reproduce byte-identically, and 17,721 independent exact controls pass. Its complement has a connected double cover with nonzero third homology, obstructing every Weinstein structure.

The construction builds on the prior Auroux example presented by Giroux. The frozen proof passed a separate adversarial AI review with no mathematical corrections. Explicit construction

An explicit answer to Holland's Problem 5.51 (AMR-022-5051): a deterministic four-adic integer recursion produces rational finite Blaschke products B_n with algebraic coefficients. Their locally uniform limit B is an infinite Blaschke product with B(0)=0 and Bloch Cayley transform (1+B)/(1-B).

The construction includes the quantitative bound

`sup_{|z|<=r} |B(z)-B_n(z)| <= 4*pi*r*4^(-n)/(1-r)^2`.

The proof separately excludes a singular inner factor. The absorbed unit-step densities cannot converge to a finite positive value at any boundary point; Loomis's positive-measure converse Fatou theorem would force exactly such convergence if a singular factor were present. A proved global Zygmund estimate gives the Bloch property.

## Scope and prior work

- The complete explicit recursion and proof are in `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2305051/CANDIDATE.md`
- This is a recursive rational-inner construction with an effective compact-uniform error bound, not a short closed-form zero list
- Existence and stronger covering-map results were already known
- Kahane's and Cantón's martingale methods and all classical analytic inputs are credited
- Historical priority is unestablished

## Separate validation

The unchanged independent adversarial review passes the complete construction and the source's explicitness requirement, including the singular-factor argument and exact disk normalization.

- 2,884 author exact assertions, reproduced byte-for-byte
- 37,154 independent exact controls, reproduced byte-for-byte
- Frozen candidate SHA-256: `0a15d03ab92cbd13f17042a4708f75c3d592f4884810c7ffadc6a5f34f1cb6c4`

The finite controls support, but do not replace, the all-stage and analytic proof. This is separate AI review, not human peer review. Please keep this PR open as a draft for further examination.

Exact scope

Records an affirmative answer to the literal per-element additive-distortion condition in Calegari's Question 8.2. This is a credited consequence of known line-action conjugacy results, not a new discovery.

Deroin–Kleptsyn–Navas–Parwani, Ann. Probab. 41 (2013), Theorem 8.5, gives a stronger conclusion for finitely generated orientation-preserving actions. The package includes self-contained deterministic proofs of the needed weaker conclusion, including a countable-family, orientation-reversing extension. All maps use one common coordinate change.

The historical toroidal-obstruction remark is explicitly retained as a mismatch with the displayed quantifiers. No bound uniform across group elements, geometric control of the conjugacy, or ambient leaf-distance conclusion is asserted.

## Validation

- 6,665 exact rational author controls
- Separate adversarial AI review PASS, with 20,173 independent exact checks
- Full original problem PDF, earlier published formulation and current published-theorem reprint checked
- No novelty claim or new-solution campaign credit

Recommended queue classification: `already_solved` for the literal statement. The parent coordinates the queue row; this branch changes only the problem's attempt directory.

The reduced denominator contains precisely the factors associated with nonzero algebraic vertices, whose tangent-cone indicators are not signed sums of line-cone indicators.

This package matches that result to the original triangulation-intersection vertex convention, supplies the explicit pole calculation and finite cone-flipping interpretation, and preserves the origin exception: the factor for the origin is the constant 1. This draft contains a complete candidate negative answer to the specified conformal-metric parametrization question for every finite integer r>=0, on both the plane and the sphere.

The counterexample sequences consist of smooth complete strictly positive-curvature metrics converging in C^r, while their uniquely normalized conformal diffeomorphisms fail to converge in C^(r+1). The r=1 endpoint includes an exact nonlinear curvature-preserving correction; curvature continuity in C^1 is not assumed.

The proof concerns this particular parametrization. It does not rule out other product homeomorphisms, and it does not contradict the known Hölder or C-infinity statements. The source's 2016 erratum and exact derivative shift are documented.

This preserves two unsuccessful approaches to Calegari's Question 7.1 (Agol), asking for a characterization of embedded branched surfaces that admit a nontrivial self-splitting.

The original question has general embedded scope; the triangulation in its following remark is auxiliary. The invariant-measure observation and pseudo-Anosov examples are already in the source and are credited as prior work.

## Exact remaining gaps

- No construction of a legal embedded self-splitting and return homeomorphism from transverse-weight cone data
- No reduction from arbitrary self-splitting carriers to the prescribed depth-one, Handel–Miller, and veering hypotheses of the restricted literature
- No unbounded splitting-radius estimate for the prescribed iterates, nor a construction extending the particular partial lamination

The artifact proves the standard finite-dimensional cone lemma and gives explicit algebraic controls showing why stronger matrix shortcuts do not follow. Those matrices are not claimed to have geometric realizations. The full classification remains unresolved after two approaches.

## Separate review

The unchanged adversarial review passes this explicitly unresolved source-scope and obstruction package. Both exact check receipts reproduce byte-for-byte: 191 author assertions and 1,141 independent algebraic controls. This is AI review, not human peer review, and no novelty is claimed.

A combinatorial proof of the projected discriminant/Hurwitz weight-polytope comparison requested by OWR-14299288-015, in the smooth, complete very ample, degree-at-least-two regime of the source's cited Sano theorem.

The argument combines a product-face centroid identity, finite-difference cancellation, equal-column regular refinements, and the established GKZ normal-fan compatibility. The support-function step proves the reverse inclusion without assuming that every projected discriminant vertex remains a vertex. The previously known geometric equality, GKZ foundations, Sano's analytic description, and Ogusu–Sano's surface inclusion are credited.

## Scope

- The complete proof is in `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30006309/CANDIDATE.md`
- Smoothness, complete lattice-point embeddings, and the source's degree hypothesis are retained
- This is a combinatorial comparison within established GKZ theory, not a reconstruction of its foundations
- Arbitrary singular or incomplete configurations are outside the claim
- Historical novelty is unestablished

## Independent validation

A separate adversarial review passes the complete intended comparison and explicitly checks both the restored source hypotheses and requested proof type. The unchanged report and source-verification receipt are included under `review/`.

- 1,227 author exact assertions, reproduced byte-for-byte
- 8,093 independent exact lower-hull assertions, reproduced byte-for-byte
- Frozen mathematical artifact SHA-256: `4931eccbb464b53af07b90e24b72060e681b9a7f1769c0030a9d7090e59b129c`

The finite checks are diagnostics alongside the general proof. This is separate AI review, not human peer review. Please keep this PR open as a draft for further examination.

Partial result; original Hudson problem remains unsolved

This package preserves the exact source's linear-subdivision and prescribed-target conditions. It gives an elementary equivalence with the protected-boundary problem for one subdivided simplex, and reconstructs a constructive relative-collapse certificate in dimensions at most two. These are credited low-dimensional/reduction facts, with no novelty claim.

The general higher-dimensional problem is not solved. The dual-tree method leaves a higher-dimensional contractible residual for which no relative free-face sequence is supplied. Adiprasito–Benedetti's published theorem adds a barycentric subdivision to both complexes; it is credited and not substituted for the original target. A general PL ball or a nonshellable triangulation is not asserted to be a counterexample.

## Independent review and exact certificates

A separate adversarial review passed the frozen partial result, with no required mathematical corrections. The author checker passes 4,200 exact rational/face-set assertions over 27 disk meshes and six gluing controls. Independent verification passes 59,718 invariant assertions over 387 disk-target cases, 387 external-gluing cases and 30 interval cases. Counts include repeated invariants at successive moves; these are not high-dimensional search results.

An explicit small certificate and both review receipts are included. Run `python3 unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30002061/verify.py` with the Python standard library.

Actual model: gpt-6-astra, xhigh. One substantive family, stopped at the precise relative-collapse gap. Recommended queue status: unsolved, 1/5. The coordinator owns queue edits.

Already solved in the cited original source

The exact Q-algebra reduction-map surjectivity theorem was proved by Arno van den Essen, Stefan Maubach and Stéphane Vénéreau, JPAA 210 (2007), 141–146, DOI 10.1016/j.jpaa.2006.09.013. The original OWR report p.26 explicitly answers YES immediately after the extracted question; the 2007 Acta problem collection independently confirms every commutative unital ring containing Q and all m,n≥1.

This is a source-curation correction, with no new discovery claim. Recommended queue status: already_solved, 0/5 new proof-search attempts. The coordinator owns the queue edit.

## Checked proof and scope

The package gives a fully credited self-contained reconstruction: divergence-free vectors decompose into exact special shears, and finite t-adic corrections lift the prescribed automorphism. Arbitrary nonreduced Q-algebras are included. There is no assumption that a Jacobian-one endomorphism is automatically invertible and no assertion that every base-ring automorphism is tame.

The full OWR and Acta sources were recovered and their decisive pages visually checked. The full JPAA journal article was not recovered; this access limitation remains explicit. The reconstruction is not described as a line-by-line audit of that unavailable paper.

## Independent review

A separate adversarial review passed the exact source scope and proof, including nonlinear, nilpotent-ring and zero-divisor controls. All 211 author assertions and 142 independent assertions passed. The final header-only proof hash is covered by the review. Actual model: gpt-6-astra, xhigh.

Run `python3 unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30000644/verify.py` with SymPy 1.14.0. The review folder also retains the frozen snapshot needed to replay its copied submitted verifier.

Correct the real-periodic rational-map interior status (30004438)

## Existing result

The full nonempty-interior question was answered by Kozhasov–Kummer in arXiv:2004.10003v1, Theorem 2 (April 2020), and remains covered by the current v2. This package corrects the imported assessment that only lower-dimensional families were known. It claims no new discovery and does not claim a verified journal publication.

## Verification

The original OWR Questions 1–2 and both preprint versions were checked. The known construction is spelled out in the full real projective coefficient chart, with an all-iterate argument. All 51 exact controls pass. No statement about the Hermite conjecture or higher-dimensional projective space is implied.

Separate source/mathematical review passed the exact frozen artifact with no mandatory correction. All 848 independent exact controls pass. The package is AI-reviewed and unrefereed. Shared queue changes belong to the coordinator; recommended status is already_solved with existing-author credit.

Scoped partial result; original target remains unsolved

This package proves the expected in-square spanning-network length is asymptotic to ell·k under the usual SIRSN axioms. It also proves the full, untruncated asymptotic under the extra condition t^4 P(D1>t)→0, in particular when the unit-distance route length has finite fourth moment.

The proof separately controls the exterior: a dyadic major-road intensity estimate handles bounded excursions, while a pair-route tail estimate handles the far exterior. It includes the Poisson-to-binomial conversion. The first-moment assumption in the original axioms has not been shown to imply the added tail bound, so the unconditional problem remains unresolved.

## Exact source corrections

Span is the union of all prescribed pairwise routes, not a Steiner-minimal subnetwork. Ell is the edge intensity of the rate-one Poisson sampled network. The source is Open Problem 35 in the 2012 manuscript, but Open Problem 9 in the published 2014 paper, which explicitly asks which extra assumptions, if any, suffice. The historical imported report is preserved alongside these corrections.

Current model and geodesic literature is credited with its precise scope. No historical-priority or full-solution claim is made.

## Review and checks

The separate adversarial review passed the precise conditional scope, with 3,809 independent exact controls, and is included before this draft opens. The author checker passes 211 exact algebraic/distributional controls. These are finite diagnostics, not a SIRSN simulation or a verification of the missing general case.

Run: `python3 unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/9700035/verify.py` with SymPy 1.14.0.

Actual research model: gpt-6-astra at xhigh. Two substantive attempts, then a precise stop at the distant-excursion integrability gap. Recommended queue status is unsolved; the coordinator handles the queue row.

The original bounded Brownian concatenation problem remains **unsolved**. This partial proves an almost-sure approximation by fixed-origin two-sided Brownian motion with O(sqrt(log R)) uniform error on [-R,R], hence a two-sided diffusive scaling limit. It does not establish the exact finite random time shift required by the original definition.

## Scope and review
- Independent, not necessarily identically distributed, stopped Brownian pieces; a common deterministic duration bound and divergent sums in both directions
- Explicit treatment of zero durations and of the distinction between a fixed junction and a random time origin
- Piece-rotation mechanism credited to Burdzy and Scheutzow; no novelty or priority claim
- Separate adversarial review passed the unchanged frozen mathematical artifact, with the submitted and independent exact controls included

Two substantive attempts used. Actual author and reviewer model: gpt-6-astra, xhigh. This is a scoped partial research checkpoint, not a full solution.

Scope clarification and partial reductions

The substantive closed genus-at-least-two version of KP2.17 remains **unsolved**. This package does not classify currents having the full hyperbolic length function of an arbitrary self-intersecting closed geodesic.

It records the exact all-metric Liouville-intersection fiber, the classical reduction to measured-lamination intersection data (whose converse fails), compact convex fibers, and rigidity for a simple reference curve. Compactness and finite matrix tests are not substituted for a finite-support theorem.

There is a scoped counterexample under the complete finite-area punctured-surface convention: the thrice-punctured sphere has singleton Teichmüller space, and a scaled non-atomic Liouville current matches any chosen nonperipheral closed-geodesic length. This convention must be distinguished from a compact-core current space or a pair of pants with variable boundary lengths. The K3 book's broad chapter conventions and the problem's unstated closedness make this a source-scope issue; no campaign closed-surface solution or historical-priority credit is claimed.

The actual original question is in the K3 book, printed pp.98–99. The dataset's AIM URL points only to a four-page workshop summary. Full source pointers, the current Leininger/Jyothis equivalence distinctions and the noncompact-current caveat are included.

## Review and checks

Separate adversarial mathematical/source review passed for this explicitly partial scope, with 72 independent exact assertions. It is included before this draft opens. Run `python3 unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2765/verify.py` (SymPy1.14.0). It passes 30 exact matrix/free-word controls, including the explicit hyperbolic Γ(2) element and a generic trace-reversal identity. These are not finite tests of the full all-Teichmüller-space current condition.

Actual model: gpt-6-astra xhigh. Two substantive attempts, then a precise stop at the closed-surface finite-support/convex-decomposition gap. The coordinator owns the QUEUE update to unsolved.

Record planar consequence and unresolved higher-dimensional gap (3009)

The complete KP-5.2 target remains unsolved. This package supplies a credited proof of the dimension-one and planar cases, including the boundary-fixed closed disk, from established Cartwright–Littlewood and Kolev–Pérouème results. The disk consequence was already stated in the 1998 paper. No discovery or full-resolution credit is claimed.

The proof explicitly checks orientation, recurrence at infinity, filled-continuum invariance, and the distinction between compact-open and Euclidean-uniform recurrence. It does not assume equicontinuity or a compact cyclic closure. The higher-dimensional homeomorphism and smooth-recurrence variants remain unresolved here.

One substantive response used; 31 exact algebraic controls pass. Separate adversarial review passed the frozen artifact with no mandatory correction; 8,462 independent exact assertions pass. The work is AI-reviewed and unrefereed. Shared queue update handled by the coordinator.

A complete, independently reviewed negative answer to the pinned AIM question: a graph-defined degree-11 algebraic critically fixed rational-map class has field of moduli contained in the reals in the chosen embedding, but no real model. It therefore has no model over its field of moduli.

The construction uses the established critically fixed plane-graph classification. The proof supplies the intrinsic symmetry action, an actual invariant charge graph, the reflection obstruction, algebraicity and the field-of-moduli argument. Historical novelty and minimal degree are unestablished. No coefficient list, exact number field, or total-reality claim is made.

- Author verifier exhausts 1,152 degree-compatible vertex permutations
- Independent verifier passes 183 exact assertions; both receipts reproduced exactly
- Review Section 6 explicitly justifies algebraic conjugators

The finite checks do not replace the mathematical proof. Independent AI review is not formal verification or peer review.

## Source limits

For 6800007 / AMR-067-0007, the manuscript gives an explicit integral-cohomology classification of homotopies through totally real immersions of a fixed smooth real 3-manifold into the ordered complex full flag manifold. The indices are pairs of degree-two classes satisfying an orientation-Bockstein condition. Each fiber is a torsor for a degree-three cohomology group plus the cokernel of an explicit cup-product homomorphism. This computes the coupled monodromy action, rather than only restating the known h-principle or counting framings over a fixed map.

The source audit fixes the graph and bond-percolation conventions, credits the known bounded-cutset special case, and records why a stretched-tree example and an inhomogeneous ray block the attempted reductions. These examples do not refute the original question.

A separate adversarial AI review passed the frozen partial proof with no mandatory correction. Scoped partial theorem

Candidate nonlinear **W^{1,∞} orbital instability** of the peaked periodic reduced Ostrovsky wave, in a directly constructed single-corner characteristic solution class. The proof builds local evolution including one-sided derivatives, gives a slope-bounded continuation criterion, controls the true moving-corner value, and forces a fixed slope-norm departure on a logarithmic time scale.

**The original low-regularity source problem is not declared solved.** This is not an L² or H¹ orbital-instability theorem. It does not establish finite-time blow-up or select/uniquely define weak continuations after breakdown. The campaign's full-target status remains unresolved/partial.

## Prior work and review

- Exact OWR 32/2019 contribution, printed pp.1940–1942, checked
- Established Geyer–Pelinovsky linear/spectral results credited
- Superseded arXiv:1804.03788v1 nonlinear claim preserved in source history; it was removed in v2/published2019 and is not used as a theorem
- The recent Hunter–Saxton-related model is distinguished from the reduced Ostrovsky equation
- Historical novelty unconfirmed; no external peer-review or formal-verification claim
- Model and effort: gpt-6-astra, xhigh; one substantive response used

Separate adversarial AI review: **PASS for the scoped strong-norm theorem**, with no required mathematical correction. All **20** submitted checks and **135** independent assertions passed. Frozen reviewed SHA-256: `95458afe7f030f3f0aec3b9d5150857e7dedcb8688e6325c4a0407497feb1b6c`. The full independent report is included in the problem package. Exact checks supplement the analytic argument and do not establish the PDE result by finite testing.

All changes are confined to `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004186/`. No shared queue/state/catalog edit, merge, routine release, or outreach is included. This is the one draft PR for this problem.

For a C^{2,alpha} convex surface with constant-area strips of one fixed width h, the note proves spherical rigidity under the extra condition h < twice the inradius. Averaging centered strips over orientations makes the uniform surface-charge Newtonian potential constant on a nonempty open interior set. Harmonic continuation and Reichel's classical electrostatic rigidity theorem then imply a sphere.

The original question assumes only h < diameter. The range h >= twice the inradius, and any nonsmooth-boundary extension, remain unresolved. No campaign solved credit or historical-priority claim is made. Keep QUEUE status **unsolved**.

## Source scope and obstruction

Ghomi's own 2017 formulation explicitly assumes a convex surface. The shorter 2019 wording sits under a convex-surfaces heading. A disconnected nested-sphere example is recorded solely to explain why exploiting the abbreviated wording would not resolve the intended target. The note also isolates the inadequate periodic-density inference and gives a tetrahedron control showing that minimum width > h does not imply the additional inradius condition.

A separate adversarial review is included before opening this draft. The verifier passes 1,056 exact normalization, support-width, and excluded-example checks; these supplement the proof and are not a certificate for the external rigidity theorem or the full open problem.

Adds 13 compressed archives (594 MiB total), a 0.65 MiB universal-amplification history bundle, per-file checksums, recovery instructions, and a completed cleanup log. Existing GitHub content is referenced by exact Git blob ID instead of duplicated.

This is an archival PR; recovered experiments and historical manuscripts have not been promoted as validated results. Borsuk working changes, universal-amplification experiments, STC-JC v1.1.5 artifacts, Kissing-5 snapshots, K2P referee outputs, and Ramsey certificates are included.

Validation: every archive member matched its original SHA-256 checksum. Every uploaded file was then streamed back from GitHub and its SHA-256 verified. Sources were rechecked immediately before deletion. The history bundle was verified by Git.

Cleanup completed: removed the universal-amplification clone and STC-JC worktree, removed 35,136 inventoried local files plus disposable runtimes, and consolidated four identical oversized K2P copies. The primary Math checkout was untouched by this task.

Remaining local material totals approximately 844 MiB: Borsuk Git metadata (4.1 MiB, retaining eight commits outside main), the Kissing-5 untracked archive (108 MiB), private YBE files and three oversized Ramsey files (527 MiB), and one oversized K2P archive (205 MiB). Exact retained paths and checksums are in CLEANUP_RESULT.json. The Borsuk history bundle alone was 1.18 GiB, so that history was retained locally rather than added as a GitHub file.

What changed

- Adds Discovery 7, **“A 14-variable unipotent Keller map and every-order image and vanishing obstructions.”**
- Makes one inverse-series mechanism—not a conjecture tally—the paper’s intellectual center:
  - Abhyankar–Gurjar transfer gives failure of `SIC(14)` at every positive exponent.
  - Symmetric/Hessian transfer plus Zhao’s inverse formula gives nonvanishing of `Delta^m(P^(m+1))` at every order.
- Consolidates the strongest parts of Discoveries 3, 5, and 6 while preserving their PDFs, hashes, timestamps, and technical derivations.
- Keeps Discovery 4 as the separate current iterated-monodromy paper.
- Adds the canonical website page, PDF, scope/priority audit, research log, deterministic JSON certificate, and three exact checkers.

## Headline artifacts

- Exact 24-term 14-variable vector with determinant pencil one, generic Jordan type `(14)`, and an exact reduced rational three-point fiber.
- Every-exponent `SIC(14)` obstruction.
- 28D nonhomogeneous and 30D homogeneous degree-eight Hessian companions.
- 44D homogeneous quartic with a nonzero Vanishing obstruction at every order.
- Exact weighted conjugacy, homogeneous type `(14,1)`, and coefficient-by-coefficient matches against the pinned Discovery 3 and 6 certificates.

The manuscript explicitly treats the Campbell, Chamberland–Meisters, and Kulikov implications as one transformation cascade rather than independent discoveries. It also records that prior work already established the existential Image/Vanishing consequences; the candidate contribution here is the small explicit fixed-dimensional and every-order realization.

## Verification

- `verify_symbolic.py`: all 9 exact checks passed in 30.25 s; maximum RSS 77,053,952 bytes (about 74 MiB); zero swaps.
- `verify_exported_stdlib.py`: passed.
- `verify_exported_node.mjs`: passed independently with Node.js/BigInt.
- Unified JSON SHA-256: `deb01a83cea8543b17c13e8849cead0159d5d8feac07ae18034fd880a274495c`.
- PDF built reproducibly with Tectonic; all 11 rendered pages visually inspected.
- All local website links and the published PDF copy were checked.

- add Discovery 06: an explicit 24-term map in 14 variables with everywhere-unipotent Jacobian, generic Jordan type `(14)`, a rational three-point fiber, and an every-exponent `SIC(14)` witness

- add a separate bounded-memory level-four proof artifact, establishing `Mon(F^4)=W_4` from a good-reduction certificate at `p=1009, s=801`
- refresh the research index, paper pages, PDFs, archive labels, and sitemap

## Exact verification

- Discovery 06 symbolic suite: PASS in 4.89 s, 61,095,936-byte max RSS

- independent `W_4` exact-determinant audit: PASS under 50 MB
- both PDFs compile without layout warnings; all 6 and 9 pages were visually inspected
- publication pages render without horizontal overflow or console errors; all local links and PDFs resolve

## Review focus

All claims remain provisional and unreviewed. The most valuable expert checks are:

1. the every-exponent `SIC(14)` inversion formula and the narrow priority language;
2. the `W_3` multiplicity-one discriminant divisor and reconstruction guards;
3. the `W_4` Hensel/localization step, etale norm-valuation argument, and resulting single-leaf inertia.

exact_target_matches.title: 10400115: reviewed braid specialization obstruction; target unresolved
exact_target_matches.body:
The generic-to-algebraic specialization route does not settle Bigelow's faithful-representation question. This package records the exact source, restriction of scalars from algebraic to rational coefficients, an explicit example in which every algebraic specialization loses faithfulness, and the corrected rational representation for three strands.

The full target remains unresolved for n ≥ 4. No novelty or general nonexistence claim is made. Independent adversarial review passed for this partial scope. The author verification receipt reproduced exactly, and 35 additional exact matrix checks passed.

All changes are confined to the problem's attempt directory, including the frozen note, source provenance, research log, checks and independent review.
